Using Householder--LKS synthesis, the circuit prepares each symmetry-allowed reduced block and applies Clebsch--Gordan coefficients to recover the magnetic degrees of freedom, avoiding explicit loading of the corresponding unfolded dense tensors. The reduced-tensor data loading is dominant in cost. We benchmark $4 \times 4$ and $4 \times 6$ Fermi--Hubbard states and active-space models of \ce{[Fe2S2]^2-}, \ce{[Fe4S4]^2-}, and low- and high-spin cytochrome P450. At 15-bit rotation precision, the molecular benchmarks show $\sim 14\times$ to $54\times$ Toffoli reductions, $\sim 20\times$ to $87\times$ active volume reduction, and $\sim 33\times$ to $140\times$ volume (Toffoli $\times$ qubits) reduction at the QROM-optimal point, relative to dense MPS loading. Fermi--Hubbard speedups increase with bond dimension and track the inverse tensor density, with modest qubit overhead. However, while we discuss generalization of our algorithm to reduce cost given further symmetry or using more performant unitary synthesis methods, extrapolation to larger lattices suggests that DMRG-state loading may exceed downstream phase-estimation costs, motivating co-design of state fidelity, compression, and the initial-state ansatz.

papers.title: State Diagram of Dual-Free-Layer Perpendicular Magnetic Tunnel Junctions for Artificial Spiking Neurons
papers.abstract: The performance of perpendicular magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) depends critically on interfacial properties and layer thicknesses, small variations of which can substantially modify their magnetic and transport characteristics. This work investigates, experimentally and numerically, a perpendicular MTJ with two free layers, a configuration that preserves the precessional dynamics of the device while simplifying its fabrication. Quasi-static state diagrams measured under magnetic fields and DC or pulsed bias reveal static parallel, antiparallel, and bistable regimes, as well as a dynamical windmill regime in which the reversal of one layer triggers that of the other, giving rise to spiking neuron-like signals. Macrospin simulations reproduce these diagrams, and a stability analysis of the Landau-Lifchitz-Gilbert (LLG) equation yields an analytical description of the critical lines, including the windmill threshold voltage. The comparison also reveals a quadratic term in the voltage dependence of the spin-transfer torque that Joule heating cannot explain. The analytical model shows that the threshold voltage can be lowered either by approaching the spin-reorientation transition, at the cost of thermal stability, or by enhancing the quadratic contribution to the spin-transfer torque. These results establish guidelines for optimizing multilayer MTJ stacks for artificial spiking neurons and a broader range of neuromorphic and spintronic applications.

papers.title: Eclipse-minimising sun-synchronous orbits in a mean-Sun rotating frame
papers.abstract: A satellite in low Earth orbit normally passes through Earth's shadow on every revolution. A dawn-dusk sun-synchronous orbit largely avoids it: J2 precession keeps the orbit plane facing the Sun all year, but it follows only the Sun's average position, the mean Sun. In reality the Sun wanders up to 23 degrees around this average, enough to push the plane into shadow for part of the year. We introduce MSSI, a coordinate frame that rotates with the mean Sun. In it, a sun-synchronous orbit is a fixed ring and the real Sun traces the analemma, so the yearly eclipse question becomes static geometry. From that picture we derive how much of each orbit is in shadow, the yearly eclipse for every plane orientation, maps of which directions are never, sometimes or always eclipsed, and the margin a mission has. Fixed planes become eclipse-free above about 1400 km, within a window of node offsets that widens with altitude, and the 06:00 and 18:00 lines turn out to be equivalent. The closed form is checked against a full-force-model numerical propagation and against the published eclipse seasons of three flying missions; the model, its code and an interactive 3-D visualizer are published as open source.

papers.title: The Cost of Quantum State Conversion
papers.abstract: Which losses in quantum-state preparation can better control remove, and which are imposed by the available resources? We determine the least entropy production for converting known full-rank states using fresh thermal auxiliaries of fixed size and bounded energy range, with arbitrary driven joint control. For every reachable target, the asymptotic infimum is the decrease of a computable function of the state's spectrum. Explicit finite protocols approach this limit, including at saturated resource constraints. The result therefore supplies an attainable benchmark for state preparation, rather than only a lower bound. Reusable memory changes both reachability and the cost without enlarging any fresh auxiliary. A uniform memory gives an exact rescaling of the resource parameter; all memory states preparable from it under the same constraint have the same reachable targets and asymptotic costs. Externally supplied biased memories can do better, revealing a preparation resource distinct from dimension. With sufficient fixed memory, protocols reach exact product endpoints while dissipation decreases inversely with operation count. These results connect algorithmic cooling, quantum resource theories, and constructive control by separating unavoidable loss from the overhead of a chosen implementation.

papers.title: TOI-2665 b: A Highly Irradiated Giant in the Hot Neptune Desert
papers.abstract: We report the confirmation of TOI-2665 b, a close-in sub-Saturn ($P=2.85$ days, $R_p=7.00_{-0.15}^{+0.16}~R_{\oplus}$) just inside the hot Neptune desert around a metal-rich G dwarf, observed by the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS). We make use of the Carnegie Planet Finder Spectrograph for precise radial velocity measurements to measure its mass with $13.5σ$ precision ($M_p= 57.0_{-4.2}^{+4.2} ~M_{\oplus}$). The low density of TOI-2665 b ($ρ_{p} \sim 0.9~\mathrm{gcm}^{-3}$) implies the existence of a significant gaseous envelope that has survived in the hot Neptune desert despite high irradiation ($S=1068~S_{\oplus}$), making it an intriguing target for understanding the formation and evolution of desert-dwelling giants. The relatively bright host star ($V=11.0$ mag, $J=9.8$ mag) and extensive atmosphere make TOI-2665 b a promising target for atmospheric characterization.

papers.title: Thouless's bandwidth conjecture: a proof by elliptic periods
papers.abstract: We prove Thouless's bandwidth conjecture for the critical rational Harper operator: the denominator times the total bandwidth tends to $32G/π$, uniformly in the reduced numerator, where $G$ is Catalan's constant. We identify a universal limit of the normalized even coarea density. Positive real part and evenness give an integrable endpoint bound, so the local law determines the bandwidth. An exact finite-matrix formula reduces the local law to one normalized period for each fixed odd numerator. Explicit boundary polynomials, point blowups, and intersections determine a compact genus-one family. Nodal-annulus calculations fix its period equation and hence the universal density. An exact rational Fourier identity and uniform closed-path bounds extend the result to all reduced numerators and both denominator parities. The singular matrix limit, including its subtraction and normalization, is proved separately in detail.

papers.title: MIAO: Microscaling Intermediate Accumulation Optimization
papers.abstract: Microscaling (MX) quantization enables lower-precision large language model (LLM) inference with limited accuracy degradation, reducing memory requirement and multiplication cost. However, despite reduced operand precision, accumulation is often retained at high floating-point precisions, leaving a substantial hardware cost that operand quantization alone does not address. In particular, systolic arrays, as used in tensor accelerators such as Google TPU and AWS Trainium, distribute accumulation across distinct processing elements but conventionally use uniform accumulator precision throughout the array. This spatial organization offers an opportunity to reduce hardware cost by tailoring precision to individual accumulation stages. In this work, we present MIAO, a hardware-software co-design framework that jointly selects product precision and stage-dependent accumulator widths to minimize hardware area and energy cost under an end-to-end perplexity constraint. MIAO first calibrates MX block-scale shifts to reduce intermediate magnitudes while preserving operand quantization accuracy, then assigns narrower accumulators to earlier stages and progressively wider accumulators to later stages. To efficiently explore the resulting design space, MIAO combines hardware cost estimates derived from logic synthesis with a calibrated accuracy predictor to identify promising precision configurations, then validates the accuracy of promising candidates through bit-exact end-to-end LLM evaluation. Across MXFP8, MXFP6, and MXFP4, MIAO reduces processing element (PE) array area by up to 38.7% and energy by up to 36.1% relative to the all-BF16 accumulation baseline, with at most 1.60% additional perplexity degradation over operand-only MX quantization across six LLMs.

papers.title: Magnetogenesis in Low-Scale Inflation: Viability for Astrophysical Magnetic Fields
papers.abstract: The indirect evidence for magnetic fields in the intergalactic medium motivates the study of their possible primordial origin, including generation during inflation. One mechanism for inflationary magnetogenesis involves a pseudoscalar inflaton coupled to a gauge field through the interaction $g_{ϕγ}ϕF_{μν}\tilde{F}^{μν}$. In this work, we study the viability of this mechanism in the context of low scale inflation, particularly on inflationary energy scales near the electroweak (EW) scale. We find that the post inflationary amplification of the gauge fields can produce astrophysically relevant magnetic fields for $g_{ϕγ}\ge 360~m_{\rm pl}^{-1}$ in the absence of Schwinger backreaction for an inflationary scale around the EW scale. We then include the backreaction of the charged current generated through the Schwinger mechanism. We find that the induced current suppresses the gauge field amplification and leads to a saturation of the gauge field energy density at a value of order $m_e^4$, where $m_e$ is the electron mass. Assuming this saturation level, we find that magnetic fields above the lower bound inferred from the non detection of secondary GeV photons from blazars can be obtained when reheating occurs at temperatures below $\sim 0.3$ GeV. For an inflationary energy scale of $100~{\rm GeV}$, achieving this saturation until a reheating temperature, $T\le 0.3~{\rm GeV}$, requires a coupling strength $g_{ϕγ}\ge 20000~m_{\rm pl}^{-1}$. We obtain a present-day magnetic field strength of $B_0 \sim 2\times10^{-13}$ G with a coherence length of $L_{0}\sim 5\times10^{-3}$ kpc for the reheating temperature of $100$ MeV.

papers.title: Sim-to-Real Room-Mediated Object-Goal Navigation with ROS 2 and Nav2
papers.abstract: Although object-goal navigation (ObjectNav) approaches are usually evaluated in simulation, which offers scale and repeatable environments, real-world deployments are rarely examined beyond feasibility demonstrations. This paper presents the deployment of Room-Mediated Co-occurrence, an ObjectNav policy that reasons over Room Probability Vectors (RPVs), on two robotic platforms (Boston Dynamics Spot and Clearpath Robotics TurtleBot 4) through a robot-agnostic ROS 2 bridge. We study how these semantic priors generalise to physical environments and describe the adaptations required to transfer RPV from simulation to hardware, covering sensing, localisation, and the action interface. Across 66 trials on Spot, searching for 11 object categories from two starting positions in a university postgraduate research facility, RPV achieves a raw Success Rate (SR) of 0.455. Our analysis identifies undetected glass walls, entry into off-limits areas, limited usable depth range, target size, and mismatch between the room lexicon and physical layout as plausible contributors to the 8.4 percentage-point gap between the real-world SR and the reported simulated SR of 0.539. Code is available at https://github.com/Matthew-K-Chua/rpv-ros2-bridge.

papers.title: Found, but Not Fixed : From Software Vulnerability Discovery to Fixes with Iterative LLM Pipelines
papers.abstract: Software vulnerabilities persist as a critical threat despite the deployment of sophisticated detection tools and AI assistants. While detection has advanced, the subsequent code repair phase remains a primary bottleneck; manual intervention is inherently slow, costly, and prone to introducing secondary regressions and issues. In this paper, we investigate whether an iterative, LLM-based pipeline can provide a robust solution for the automated repair of vulnerable functions in real-world code. We propose a generalized framework that leverages the reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) through a multi-stage feedback loop. We benchmark this approach against state-of-the-art models, including GPT-4o, GPT-5.1, and Gemini 3 Flash, demonstrating that such a pipeline can achieve high-quality code repair. To support the broader security community, we provide our evaluation framework, fine-tuned weights, and comprehensive experimental dataset on our website: https://sites.google.com/view/llm4cve

papers.title: High Characteristic Voltage YBCO Josephson Junctions Written With a Focused Helium Ion Beam
papers.abstract: We report in-plane Josephson junctions written directly into YBa$_2$Cu$_3$O$_{7-δ}$ (YBCO) thin films with a focused helium ion beam (He FIB). The characteristic voltage $I_{\mathrm{C}}R$ of these junctions, where $I_{\mathrm{C}}$ is the Josephson critical current and $R$ is the junction resistance, sets the operating frequency and the sensitivity of the circuits built from them. A single line irradiation with a dose of \SI{500}{ions/nm} across a \SI{4}{\micro\metre} wide electrode produced a junction with $I_{\mathrm{C}}R$ of 929 \si{\micro\volt} at \SI{1.6}{K}, which is `higher than the 200 to 400 \si{\micro\volt} typical of junctions fabricated previously in our laboratory. Temperature dependent resistance, current-voltage characteristics, magnetic field modulation of the critical current, and Shapiro steps under 20.5~GHz microwave irradiation show Josephson behavior with an excess current below 5 percent of the critical current. The critical current falls steeply with temperature near the junction transition and saturates at low temperature. We attribute this behavior to a barrier at the metal insulator transition, where hopping conduction through localized states is active at finite temperature and freezes out on cooling. We describe the changes in surface preparation, sample selection, beam focusing, and sample storage that accompanied the improvement, although the present data do not separate their individual contributions. Larger characteristic voltages at these dimensions are an encouraging result for rapid single flux quantum and adiabatic quantum flux parametron logic and for superconducting quantum interference devices operating at elevated temperature.

papers.title: Fixed Points as Programs: Finite Symmetry and One-Shot State-Gate Duality in the Misty-State Calculus
papers.abstract: The same quantum object can support several logically distinct descriptions: it can be an eigenstate of an operator, a fixed point of an action, a nonstabilizer resource, or a state consumed by a gate-injection protocol. We make these relations precise in the misty-state calculus. The semantic core is a normalized superposition constructor $x\star y=\operatorname{N}(x+y)$. For any finite unitary group $G$, whenever the orbit sum is nonzero, the normalized orbit cloud $\operatorname{N}(\sum_{g\in G}U_gx)$ is fixed by every element of $G$; the involutive specialization $x\star Ux$ is therefore a certified fixed-point constructor. Applied to $U=H$ and $x=|0\rangle$, it gives the nested misty state $M=\operatorname{N}\{W,\operatorname{N}\{W,B\}\}$, the $+1$ Hadamard eigenstate. This state is not a Pauli stabilizer state; it is an H-type magic state and is Clifford-equivalent to $T|+\rangle$. We then prove an exact one-shot state-gate duality. Writing $J=XZ$ and $R_θ=e^{θJ}$, the state $M_θ=R_θ|0\rangle$ can be consumed by a Clifford controlled-$J$ injection circuit to apply either $R_θ$ or $R_θ^{-1}$ to arbitrary data. Whenever $R_θ^2$ is free, feed-forward makes the implementation deterministic. At $θ=π/8$, $R_θ^2=HZ=XH$ is Clifford, so one copy of $M$ implements one exact use of the non-Clifford gate $R=e^{πJ/8}$; conversely one use of $R$ prepares $M$ from $|0\rangle$. We formulate this as a pair of sound semantic certificates, $\operatorname{Fix}(U)$ and $\operatorname{Prog}(R)$, and separate the resulting finite symmetrization mechanism from the genuinely recursive fixed-point role of the $Y$ combinator, while identifying the exact $S$-combinator sharing pattern in $x\star Ux$. The result is a small, auditable semantics in which invariance and consumable program resources coexist without being conflated.

papers.title: Set-based State Estimation for Unknown Dynamical Systems from Noisy Output Data with Probabilistic Guarantees
papers.abstract: We develop a methodology for set-based state estimation from noisy input-output trajectories, without a predefined model structure for the unknown state dynamics or access to training state measurements. We derive a bound on the state set diameter that depends on the sensor map and leverage it as a surrogate to formulate a tractable linear program balancing state set tightness against output trajectory coverage. Combining this certificate with deterministic or probabilistically certified measurement noise sets and leveraging the results from scenario optimization with relaxation, we provide joint a posteriori probabilistic guarantees for state inclusion and state set diameter. Numerical simulations corroborate our developed theoretical guarantees.

papers.title: Proxima: Optimizing Syndrome Extraction Circuit Scheduling for Practical Quantum LDPC Codes
papers.abstract: The fault-tolerant performance of quantum error correction codes relies critically on the scheduling of parity checks in syndrome extraction circuits (SECs). For general CSS-type quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes, the vast scheduling space and intricate error-propagation patterns make it computationally prohibitive to directly optimize the logical error rate (LER) or the exact circuit-level distance ($d_{\mathrm{circ}}$). To address this challenge, we introduce Proxima, a highly effective automated SEC scheduling framework guided by a distance-related metric termed proximity. Defined directly on the detector error model (DEM), proximity quantifies the minimum number of additional faults required to complete a seed fault to an undetectable logical failure, naturally capturing arbitrary circuit-level fault mechanisms and bounding $d_{\mathrm{circ}}$ from above. Proxima synthesizes a pool of valid schedules at a target depth and ranks them by evaluating proximity within small, graph-local DEM fault subsets, progressively enlarging the subset only to break ties among top-ranked candidates. Across a broad spectrum of qLDPC code families, Proxima consistently attains low circuit depths and high circuit-level distance bounds, reducing LER by 1.4--2.6$\times$ over the strongest automated baseline and up to $40\times$ over others while generalizing robustly across noise models and decoders. Furthermore, by exploiting translational symmetry via a compact monomial representation, Proxima discovers depth-8 uniform schedules for bivariate bicycle codes that surpass even IBM's depth-7 reference schedule [Nature, 2024] by 2.1--5.1$\times$, establishing the DEM-level proximity as a practical objective for fault-tolerant compilation.

papers.title: An Interpretable Acoustic Coordinate System for Japanese Consonant Morae in Dysarthric Speech
papers.abstract: Dysarthria reduces speech intelligibility, requiring self-directed rehabilitation based on fine-grained feedback to capture gradual articulatory changes. For Japanese speakers, such feedback is naturally provided in mora units due to its distinct moraic timing and consonant-vowel structure. While recent visualization methods have explored distance-based feedback, most are limited to vowels. Extending them to consonants is challenging, as generative embeddings often smooth transient spectral structures. We propose a visualization system for Japanese consonant morae that maps articulatory deviations onto a two-dimensional space defined by temporal and spectral distances from healthy reference speech. Experiments show consistent geometric separation of consonant categories, with Silhouette Coefficients exceeding 0.5 and origin-based ROC-AUC scores above 0.86. Furthermore, evaluations using real dysarthric speech achieved a high ROC-AUC of 0.897 in screening for unclear pronunciations. Perturbation tests confirm orthogonal temporal and spectral shifts, yielding a physically interpretable mapping for rehabilitation.

papers.title: Cross-species digital xenocortication model delineates molecular correlates of human brain connectome
papers.abstract: Cross-species digital xenocortication (CSDX) model based on pairing of a human brain structure with one or more mouse brain structures was constructed and implemented to dissect the molecular correlates of the human brain connectome. Design of the CSDX model is based on the assumption that a human brain region and its named mouse counterpart occupy corresponding positions in an evolutionary conserved mammalian brain connectome plan, so that a projection strength measured between two mouse structures is informative about the relation between the two human structures paired with them. In the CSDX model, gene expression for the node was measured in the human brain, while connection strength between two nodes was measured in the mouse brain. CSDX models of different parcellations were employed to explore the potential regulatory associations of brain connectome patterns and constituents of protein-protein interaction (PPI) cascades of hybrid assembly pathways of endogenous multiprotein complexes. Metrics of continuous engagement of the PPI cascade nucleated protein dimers of CORUM multiprotein complexes have been identified as statistical components of the multivariate transcriptome-connectome associations. It accounts for additional connectome associated variations beyond the five measured axes in the 82 nodes CSDX model. Comparisons of the seven arm models of transcriptome-connectome associations demonstrate that the mouse derived model generally fits the mouse brain connectome better, while the human derived model assigns a significantly larger fraction of its transcriptome-connectome association to unique rather than net shared contributions. This study nominates elite panels of top scoring candidate protein dimers and CORUM multiprotein complexes for follow up mechanistic studies of their potential roles in structural functional features governing mammalian brain connectome.

papers.title: Behavioral Denoising: A New Perspective on Nonlinear Behavioral Control Inspired by Closed-Form Diffusion Policies
papers.abstract: Diffusion policies have become a dominant approach to imitation learning in robotics. Recent work suggests that, in the low-data regime, they largely retrieve or combine the demonstrated actions, which the closed-form diffusion policy does explicitly. This closely resembles behavioral control, where future inputs are formed as linear combinations of recorded trajectories. In this work, we make this connection precise: we show that the weights with which the closed-form diffusion policy combines the demonstrated actions are the unique solution of a regularized behavioral control problem. Building on this connection, we propose an algorithm, termed $χ^2$-projected behavioral denoising, which is a training-free method that combines nearby trajectory data with a limit on extrapolation when the data offer little support. It shows encouraging results on four nonlinear control tasks compared to recent nonlinear behavioral control methods. We hope that this connection offers a useful perspective for understanding both data-driven control and diffusion policies. Code and more visualizations can be found at https://github.com/RoboticExplorationLab/behavioral-denoising.

papers.title: On Semi-interval and Para-interval Graphs
papers.abstract: Bau and Johnson introduced semi-interval graphs and asked whether one of the two extremal sets can always be replaced by a single vertex. A negative answer to this question is given by a tree which has no such representation. It is also shown that a finite connected graph with at least two vertices is a semi-interval graph if and only if it is bipartite. Para-interval graphs, for which one extremal set consists of a single vertex, are characterized by necessary and sufficient conditions on their distance matrices. A characterization of para-interval trees is obtained, and a relation between para-interval graphs and shortest-path interval graphs is established by identifying the vertices of an extremal set. Finally, leveled graphs and the corresponding Hasse diagrams of finite partially ordered sets are considered.

papers.title: Joint Learning of Factual and Counterfactual Worlds for Causal Prior-data Fitted Networks
papers.abstract: Estimating treatment effects is central to science across many disciplines and requires counterfactual reasoning about alternative worlds. In the real world, however, each unit reveals its outcome only under the factual world. Thus, the factual and counterfactual outcomes can never be jointly learned by any model trained on real data. The problem is therefore tractable only in synthetic settings, where both worlds can be generated. Recent progress on prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) has shown that models pre-trained purely on synthetic data can transfer to real-world prediction. This paradigm has since carried over to causal effect estimation. Despite this fully synthetic setup, existing causal PFNs carry the real-world constraint into their training objective, confining learning to a single world's outcome per unit. The dependence between the two worlds is thereby lost, and the density of the treatment effect relies by default on independence, which is implausible in practice. We therefore propose joint learning, a training setup in which a causal PFN learns the joint distribution of the factual and counterfactual outcomes of each unit. From the joint distribution, we obtain both the response and the individual treatment effect densities, and at inference, we apply optimal transport across units to obtain an approximation of the average treatment effect density. Ours is therefore the first causal PFN approach to provide all three densities together while accounting for the cross-world dependence. We apply joint learning and optimal transport to existing causal PFNs and evaluate it across semi-synthetic, synthetic, and real benchmarks spanning diverse causal scenarios. The jointly trained models significantly improve upon their baselines in point estimation and uncertainty quantification in most settings, indicating that joint learning is a preferable training setup for causal PFNs.

papers.title: Cache or Denoise Less? Residual Reuse in a Flow-Matching World Action Model
papers.abstract: Flow-matching robot policies generate each action chunk through repeated network evaluations, one per denoising step. Cross-cycle caches such as C$^3$ache reuse computation from earlier replanning calls, but whether they beat simply taking fewer steps is unclear. We compare the two in Fast-WAM, a 6B-parameter world action model, on LIBERO-Goal. Two uncached steps keep the success of ten: on all 500 initial states they are non-inferior within two percentage points, for one checkpoint and noise seed. Under PyTorch's default compile mode, they also cut a replanning call on an RTX A6000 from 202 to 92 ms. This leaves little room for caching. A cache that keeps two fresh steps cannot be faster than two uncached steps: every call still encodes the images, runs the video expert and computes those two steps. Caching the first of two steps, refreshed every fourth call, saves at most 11--14% of a call by our cost model. Cached policies are also fragile. Their losses tracked the share of the flow path the cached steps cover: under Fast-WAM's current time shift, C$^3$ache's eight cached steps cover 80% of the path instead of 44%, and the cached policy succeeds on 63% of states against 95% uncached. Resampling the noise on every call cost caches covering 60% or more of the path 14--40 points. These results argue for fewer-step baselines and for testing reuse under the deployed sampler and noise settings. We release our evaluation harness, logs and a checklist.

papers.title: The Akhmediev breather for the Dysthe equation and the unstable manifold of the Stokes wave
papers.abstract: In this article we define and compute the breather of the Dysthe equation for deep water waves, the analogue of the Akhmediev breather of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation (NLS). When a single pair of modes is unstable, the unstable manifold of the Stokes wave consists of the Stokes wave and the translates and time shifts of a single solution, the breather. The construction uses only gauge and translation invariance, not integrability or a Hamiltonian structure. We use the parameterisation method to find the breather as a power series whose coefficients follow recursively from linear equations. This is not an asymptotic expansion: the series is the Taylor series of the breather itself. For deep water waves we map the envelope amplification over steepness and group length and give a simple formula, based on the linear stability analysis, that summarises it to within a few per cent. Our results agree well with Euler simulations: the edge of the instability band of the Dysthe equation lies much closer to the onset of growth than that of the NLS, and, away from the onset and below breaking, the crest and height amplifications lie less than 5% below the Euler ones.

papers.title: MOUSSE: Multilingual Overlapped Speech Separation with Predictive Uncertainty Estimation
papers.abstract: Recent generative speech separation methods have shown promising performance, yet mixtures of overlapping speech in different languages remain underexplored. To this end, we first curate MuSSeD, an English-Korean benchmark comprising two- to four- speaker mixtures across varying overlap ratios. We further propose MOUSSE, a flow matching framework that incorporates boundary-aware training and frame-wise predictive uncertainty through a permutation-invariant Gaussian negative log-likelihood. The predicted scale is further used to adapt classifier-free guidance during sampling. MOUSSE achieves 13.18 dB SI-SDRi and 0.175 ESTOIi, outperforming discriminative and flow matching-based separation baselines, with a 1.58 dB SI-SDRi improvement over the strongest model.

papers.title: Ferroelectric control of the $K$--$Γ$ valley landscape in R-stacked bilayer WSe$_2$
papers.abstract: In bilayer WSe2 the valence-band maxima at K and Γ lie within a few thermal energies of one another, and gating redistributes holes between a light and a heavy valley of different mobilities on a landscape that stays fixed. We show that rhombohedral (R) stacking moves the landscape itself. The three-fold symmetry of R stacking forbids interlayer tunneling at K but not at Γ. The K coupling is therefore exactly zero, not merely small. A fit that leaves the coupling free returns an upper bound of 0.017 meV, three orders of magnitude under k_BT at room temperature, while the Γ coupling is 361.8 meV. The polarization creates a potential step between the layers and splits the K doublet. Each K state stays on a single layer, so the K edge shifts by half of that splitting, 41.7 meV, which any tunneling would reduce. Γ barely responds. Two consequences follow from symmetry alone, whatever the size of that shift. The two registries, carrying opposite out-of-plane ferroelectric polarizations, are exact mirror images along the displacement-field axis, and reversing the polarization reverses the displacement of the landscape. Their differential-mode transconductances are equal and opposite at zero field, where the response vanishes for an ideal nonpolar reference. The stored polarization is read out as a reversal of sign and not as a difference of current. Sweeping the field is a second route to the same parity. In the ideal symmetric limit the transconductance passes through zero at the field that cancels the polarization, 1.07 V/nm, at a single temperature. Both routes are limited by the symmetry of the device more than by the band structure. Stacking also renormalizes the landscape, so the polar one is not a translated copy of the nonpolar reference. Absolute offsets follow the exchange-correlation functional. The symmetry relations do not.

papers.title: The automorphism group of the super Jordan plane
papers.abstract: We complete the description of the automorphism group of the super Jordan plane $\mathcal B$ over a field of characteristic zero, extending the classification of super-automorphisms obtained by N. Andruskiewitsch and F. Dumas in \cite{AD}. We characterize a subgroup $\mathbb L$ stabilizing two one-dimensional vector spaces and obtain two semidirect product decompositions of it. This subgroup contains all super-automorphisms and its structure motivates our main result. Precisely, we prove that $\operatorname{Aut}\mathcal B=\operatorname{Inn}\mathcal B\rtimes\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{super}}\mathcal B$, where $\operatorname{Inn}\mathcal B$ and $\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{super}}\mathcal B$ denote, respectively, the groups of inner automorphisms and super-automorphisms of $\mathcal B$. We also characterize the nilpotent elements of $\mathcal B$ and prove that every nonzero nilpotent has nilpotency index two. Furthermore, we give a geometric interpretation of three distinguished families of nilpotent elements. After degree truncation and projectivization, two of these families yield projective linear subspaces, while the third yields quadratic Veronese varieties of arbitrary dimension.

papers.title: Real-Time Air Pollution Monitoring and Tracking via Adaptive Density-Driven Multi-UAV Coordination
papers.abstract: Accurate and timely air pollution monitoring and tracking are critical for protecting public health and supporting effective environmental management. This paper presents an adaptive Density-Driven Control (D$^2$C) framework for coordinating multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to track and map dynamically evolving pollutant distributions. The proposed framework extends the D$^2$C strategy to guide UAV trajectories based on predictive pollutant propagation and dynamically updated reference densities. A sensor-driven surrogate plume update mechanism is employed, in which reference samples are propagated using locally sensed concentration gradients and wind estimates through gradient attraction, wind advection, inter-sample repulsion, and stochastic diffusion, enabling UAVs to maintain an accurate spatio-temporal representation of the pollution field. The framework utilizes a coordinated structure where individual UAVs share their local measurements with a central coordinator to maintain a unified set of reference samples, facilitating systematic target allocation and trajectory planning. Simulation results under both mild and strong wind conditions demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in terms of Sinkhorn distance. Specifically, in scenarios where the plume drifts beyond a fixed monitoring domain under high-velocity, time-varying wind fields, the tested baseline methods fail to maintain tracking, whereas the proposed D$^2$C framework successfully adapts to the evolving distribution. These findings highlight D$^2$C as an efficient and resilient solution for atmospheric monitoring in dynamic environments.

papers.title: Minimax Estimation of Discrete Distributions under Hockey-stick Divergence
papers.abstract: We initiate the study of estimating a discrete distribution with respect to the hockey-stick divergence from independent samples. We provide non-asymptotic upper and lower bounds on the minimax expected loss in terms of the alphabet size, the number of samples, and the divergence parameter. The upper bounds are achieved by add-constant estimators, while the lower bound is derived via a Bayes risk argument. Both upper bounds and lower bounds reveal a transition between polynomial and exponential regimes as the parameters of the problem vary.

papers.title: Multiaccuracy as an Error Benchmark for Learning with Distribution Shift
papers.abstract: Agnostic learning has a well-developed theory of computational and statistical complexity. For learning with distribution shift, even the choice of an appropriate error benchmark remains challenging. Testable learning with distribution shift (TDS) was introduced to develop computational foundations for this setting: using labeled training data and unlabeled test data, the learner must either produce a predictor with low test error or detect distribution shift. However, standard agnostic TDS guarantees allow a constant-factor amplification of the optimum error even when the training and test distributions coincide. They therefore do not directly recover the guarantee of classical agnostic learning. We introduce shift multiaccuracy, a stronger error benchmark inspired by multiaccuracy from algorithmic fairness. This yields a TDS formulation that becomes equivalent to multiaccuracy when there is no shift. Using a recent nontrivial reduction from agnostic learning to multiaccurate prediction from prior work, we obtain the first TDS framework that formally generalizes agnostic learning through an efficient reduction preserving the training marginal. The framework retains existing algorithmic upper bounds and inherits computational lower bounds from agnostic learning. Moreover, we establish a direct connection between our model and identity testing, yielding the first statistical characterization of agnostic TDS learning, in terms of Rademacher complexity. More broadly, we argue that shift multiaccuracy might be of independent interest in unsupervised domain adaptation, as it leads to sharper out-of-distribution generalization guarantees, and can be minimized directly, since its definition does not involve the unobserved test labels.

papers.title: Where Should LLM Agents Adapt at Test Time? In Context, in Weights, or Both
papers.abstract: LLM agents operating repeatedly in the same environment, such as a code repository, a database, or an application suite, encounter tasks that share latent structure. Experience can reveal this structure, allowing agents to reuse environment knowledge and learn from environmental feedback. Agents can adapt at test-time using this experience through two channels: retaining it in context and updating their weights. These channels are usually studied separately, leaving unclear what each contributes and when they complement each other. We compare in-context learning (ICL), reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards using GRPO, and self-distillation using SDPO, alone and in combination, using a shared online protocol and modular framework. Agents encounter matched task streams, are evaluated on each task before adapting to it, and learn only from their own attempts and environment feedback. We evaluate 14 adaptation mechanisms and a stateless baseline with Qwen3.5-9B on 109 tasks from four environments drawn from SWE-bench Verified, AppWorld, ScienceWorld, and BIRD-Critic-SQLite, using five task orders per environment. ICL provides the largest standalone gain: its best policy raises mean success across environments from 28.8% to 49.4%. Adding GRPO to this policy achieves the highest mean success, 51.6%. While adding GRPO improves the overall mean under every ICL policy, SDPO has mixed effects. Trace analyses show fewer lookups and shorter attempts under ICL, consistent with reusing knowledge of the shared structure. However, ICL also frequently skips inspection and verification for the current task. Adding GRPO to ICL helps restore these behaviors while preserving its reduced environment lookups. These observations suggest that reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards can refine how agents use retained experience, motivating the joint study of context management and weight updates.

papers.title: A simplified temporal logic completeness proof
papers.abstract: A temporal logic discussed in the author's book "Logics of Time and Computation" is given a simpler proof of semantic completeness, eliminating some flaws in the original.

papers.title: Data Attribution Should Steer Pretraining
papers.abstract: Pretraining data curation decides what a model learns from, yet what makes a document worth learning from depends on what the model already knows. Influence-driven selectors already rank documents to improve one run; we argue that training-data attribution should steer pretraining by identifying testable data properties that become reusable curation criteria, evaluated on new data against cheaper selectors at matched total cost, discovery included. A document ranking is consumed by the run it was computed for, whereas an explained data property can be tested across corpora and checkpoints, especially where familiar quality signals diverge from measured usefulness. Because historical contribution, an understandable explanation, and future data value require distinct evidence, we specify a feedback loop that interprets attributed sources, tests candidate data changes, and states for five claim types what evidence each requires and what none establishes. We close with a falsifiable comparison against perplexity, classifier, and mixing baselines at equal total compute.

papers.title: SPIKE-Accelerated Split-Bregman/ADMM Methods for Obstacle Problems and American Option Pricing under Jump-Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: This paper presents a parallel split Bregman/alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) \cite{goldstein,tran} for obstacle problems and for the linear complementarity problems (LCPs) that arise in the pricing of American options under the Black--Scholes and Merton jump-diffusion \cite{merton} models. The auxiliary variable of ADMM decouples the inequality constraint from the differential operator, so that every iteration consists of a linear solve with a fixed banded matrix and a pointwise projection. The matrix is factorized once by the SPIKE algorithm \cite{spike}, as in the parallel direct approach of \cite{singh}, and reused in all iterations and time steps in a Fortran~90 MPI implementation. Convergence is proved by a Lyapunov functional for every positive augmentation parameter, for the symmetric obstacle problem and the non-symmetric option LCP alike, and the iterates do not depend on the number of processes. The method therefore needs a single factorization, no tuned relaxation parameter and only pointwise, perfectly parallel updates. One- and two-dimensional obstacle problems, the Black--Scholes call and American put, and European and American options under Merton's model are computed and compared with exact, closed-form, binomial and published values. In two dimension a speed-up of $3.92$ on four processes is obtained. It is also shown that the augmentation parameter has to be scaled to the diagonal of the time-stepping matrix when only a few inner iterations are used.

papers.title: On Minima of 3D Lennard-Jones Lattice Energy and FCC-Tetragonal-Simple Hexagonal Phase Transitions
papers.abstract: Denote the Epstein zeta function by \begin{equation}\label{eq:Epstein} E(L,s):=\sum_{v\in L\setminus\{0\}}|v|^{-2s}, \;\;\hbox{where}\;\;L\;\;\hbox{is a lattice}; \qquad s>\frac32. \end{equation} We consider the three-dimensional Lennard--Jones lattice energy, which has the form \[ \mathcal E(L)=\frac12E(L,6)-E(L,3). \] We completely classify the minimizers at every covolume $|L|$, and we prove that as the covolume increases, the minimizing phase changes from the FCC to the body-centered tetragonal and then to the simple-hexagonal lattice. Thereby, we give a positive answer to an open problem raised by Blanc--Lewin [EMS Survey Series 2015, Section~2.5,~(27), pp.~268--269] and Bétermin--Petrache [JMP 2017, Question~1.15], and we prove and clarify the conjecture of Bétermin--Šamaj--Travěnec [SAM 2023].

papers.title: Equivalent-circuit analysis of the transverse resonant beam coupling impedance due to ceramic-chamber RF shields in the J-PARC Main Ring spill-feedback quadrupoles
papers.abstract: Ceramic vacuum chambers in fast-ramping or fast-response magnets are equipped with RF shields of conducting strips closed through lumped capacitors, which form a resonant circuit coupled to the transverse dipole moment of the beam. We evaluate the transverse beam coupling impedance due to the RF shields of the ceramic chambers in the spill-feedback quadrupole magnets of the J-PARC Main Ring. The RF shield is modelled by a magneto-quasi-static partial element equivalent circuit, and the laminated yoke of the magnet by a two-dimensional field solution with a complex permeability. The analysis shows a low-$Q$ resonant coupling impedance. The yoke lowers the resonance frequency and raises the shunt impedance per quality factor, and its effect cannot be neglected. The quality factor is determined mainly by the losses in the capacitors and in the laminations. The predicted peak impedance of the three chambers exceeds the resistive-wall impedance of the whole ring. The model can be applied to other machines and to the design of future rapid-cycling synchrotrons.

papers.title: Boundary regularity, finiteness and stability of energy-maximizing vortex patches
papers.abstract: We establish boundary regularity for energy-maximizing vortex patches of the 2-D incompressible Euler equations in a bounded Jordan domain. These results resolve Turkington's free-boundary regularity question throughout the full range of admissible parameters. For bounded convex domains, we further prove that the set of energy maximizers is finite at each prescribed patch area. When the domain is smooth, the number of maximizers is uniformly bounded over all admissible patch areas, and every maximizer is Lyapunov stable in $L^p$ for any $1<p<\infty$.

papers.title: Energetics of Coherent Heterophase Interfaces: Separating Chemical and Strain Contributions
papers.abstract: Coherent interfacial energies govern the formation and evolution of multiphase microstructures, but their calculation is complicated by the elastic energy required to accommodate lattice mismatch. Here, we construct a high-throughput DFT database of 365 coherent FCC/FCC, BCC/BCC, and HCP/HCP interfaces involving 41 metallic elements and lattice mismatches of up to 25%. We use the supercell approach, consisting of constructing superlattices of different thicknesses to separate the coherency strain energy from the chemical contribution to the interfacial energy. We classify the results according to the long-range ordering tendency of each binary system and the sign of the calculated interfacial energy. Most phase-separating systems exhibit positive interfacial energies, whereas most compound-ordering systems exhibit negative values, reflecting favorable unlike-atom bonding. Exceptions show that the chemical preference at a particular interface need not coincide with bulk phase behavior: coherency strain can oppose ordering, and stable compounds can adopt structures distinct from the calculated superlattices. No clear correlation of interfacial energy with lattice mismatch is observed, whereas coherency strain energy increases with mismatch. For phase-separating systems, the lowest interfacial energies generally occur along the closest-packed orientations, while this trend is absent for ordering systems. Comparisons with reported interfacial energies and binary phase diagrams show qualitative consistency, although quantitative agreement varies with reference states, structural constraints, and temperature. The database provides a systematic reference for metallic coherent heterophase interfaces and demonstrates the importance of separating strain and chemical energy contributions when interpreting alloy behavior.

papers.title: MathaMAGICal: Validating Trajectory Data Attribution During Capability Acquisition
papers.abstract: Influence-function-based methods like MAGIC provide exact first-order scores for trajectory data attribution, yet only retraining indicates whether those scores accurately predict data removal. We evaluate MAGIC on $86$M- and $152$M-parameter GPT-2-style models learning multistep arithmetic from scratch on filtered web text and four synthetic math families. Full-run attribution at $86$M suffers from numerical overflow, and even with metagradient clipping, scores correlate near chance with retraining (linear datamodeling score, LDS, $0.17$--$0.22$). In contrast, short checkpoint windows yield stable, accurate predictions at both scales (LDS $0.86$--$0.99$ across four $100$-step windows at $152$M), whereas a single-checkpoint gradient-dot baseline shows near-zero correlation. Rankings of individual training blocks predict retraining only within that single run and do not transfer across seeds or hyperparameters ($ρ\le 0.09$), whereas format-level patterns replicate across runs. Two data families, worked examples and primitive facts, occupy $2.1$--$2.6\times$ their corpus share in both the helpful and harmful $5\%$ score tails, reflecting strong bidirectional local sensitivity distinct from net benefit under multi-epoch family deletion. These results show that trajectory attribution is reliable within short, validated windows and yields family-level insights that generalize across runs.

papers.title: The structure of varieties with nef anticanonical divisor in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a regular projective variety with nef anticanonical divisor over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$, and let $f:X\to A$ be a surjective morphism to an abelian variety. We prove that there exists an isogeny $A' \to A$ such that, the base change $f': X\times_AA' \to A'$ admits a Zariski locally trivial structure. If moreover $-K_X\equiv D$ for some semiample $\mathbb Q$-divisor $D$, then $-K_X\sim_{\mathbb Q}D$, and there exists an isogeny $A' \to A$ such that, the base change $ X\times_AA' \cong X_0\times A'$ where $X_0$ is the fiber over the identity $0\in A'$.

papers.title: Comparing Two-Sample IV Estimators under Weak Instruments
papers.abstract: We compare three estimators in a two-sample summary-data instrumental variables (IV) model: inverse-variance weighting (IVW), debiased inverse-variance weighting (dIVW), and the profile score (PS) estimator. The framework assumes independent samples and instrument-specific summary estimates, with two-sample Mendelian randomisation as a leading application. We compare existing fixed- and many-weak-instrument results and the sufficient conditions for the three estimators. Under the variance scaling used in the profile-score literature, the principal collective-strength conditions for PS and dIVW are equivalent, although their additional restrictions on instrument concentration and growth differ. We then compare their asymptotic variance formulae for fixed and diverging numbers of instruments. For fixed $L$, IVW and dIVW have the same first-order asymptotic variance. Under a common variance-ratio condition, the PS variance formula exceeds the IVW variance by a positive term of order $n^{-2}$, compared with the order-$n^{-1}$ leading variance. For diverging $L$, we establish variance orders across instrument-strength regimes and the exact ordering $\mathsf{V}_{\mathtt{IVW}} < V_{\mathtt{PS}} \leq \mathsf{V}_{\mathtt{dIVW}}$ under the same variance-ratio condition. Absolute variance gaps vanish when $\sqrt{L}κ\to\infty$, whereas relative equivalence holds if and only if $κ\to\infty$. These comparisons concern asymptotic variance formulae rather than finite-sample efficiency or mean squared error.

papers.title: A generic route to chaos in self-excited plasma oscillations
papers.abstract: We propose a generic autonomous route to chaos in self-excited plasma oscillations through nonlinear feedback from a finite-rate charging variable. Near the threshold of an oscillatory ion-acoustic instability, a multiple-scale reduction yields a Stuart-Landau amplitude equation, represented by a van der Pol-type modal surrogate and coupled to debris-charge evolution in a prototype case of plasma-debris interaction scenario. For a debris-induced ion-ion counter-streaming instability, charge-dependent forcing and frequency modulation, finite charging relaxation, phase-lagged modal response, mixed nonlinear feedback, and saturation form a closed dynamical system without an externally imposed periodic driver. Numerical bifurcation and Lyapunov analyses reveal multistability and a bounded chaotic branch reached through period doubling bifurcation and band formation. We test the proposed mechanism using a one-dimensional open-boundary \emph{hybrid} particle-in-cell-Monte Carlo collision simulation incorporating particle collection, photoemission, secondary-electron emission, and surface regulation. Weak-form sparse regression identifies finite intervals whose projected dynamics reproduce the sign structure of the reduced model, while independent $0$-$1$ chaos test, nonlinear predicatbility, surrogate-data, and Lyapunov diagnostics provide localized evidence of deterministic chaotic organization in the subsonic case. The combined results establish a proof-of-principle route by which a self-excited plasma mode can become chaotic through internally generated charging feedback.

papers.title: Physics-Grounded STL Monitoring from Image Observations
papers.abstract: Robotic manipulation missions must satisfy timed and conditional requirements that can be expressed in signal temporal logic (STL). While a practical means of monitoring these requirements is from camera images, this is challenging because STL robustness depends on physical margins, such as distances and clearances, that are not directly observed. Rather than learning a separate visual monitor for each formula, we learn a shared latent representation from multi-view images and decode physically meaningful margins for individual predicates. Co-training the encoder with predicate decoders increases the certification rate from 58.7% to 96.3% compared with a frozen encoder, despite nearly unchanged predicate sign accuracy. STL semantics then compose these margins into robustness estimates for any bounded formula over the trained predicates, without retraining. We further calibrate the decoding errors of selected STL clauses using conformal prediction, yielding two-sided intervals that certify both satisfaction and violation and propagate through interval STL to any formula composed from the clauses. In simulated kitchen missions (LIBERO), our monitor correctly predicts satisfaction or violation in 98.9% of 4662 evaluations across 18 unseen formulas. For missions lasting up to 17 min, calibrated bounds establish satisfaction or violation for 96.9% of missions without incorrect conclusions. A single calibration also provides simultaneous 91.0% coverage across all 255 conjunctions of eight clauses, allowing new formulas without recalibration.

papers.title: Adaptive Precision Cholesky with Error Guarantees
papers.abstract: Modern accelerators increasingly support low-precision formats such as 8-bit floats and integers to speed up machine learning. We show that a Cholesky factorization in which both GEMM and TRSM are implemented using the fixed-point Ozaki 1 scheme satisfies the same backward error bounds as the standard floating-point Cholesky factorization, and that the same holds for a Cholesky factorization computed using a low-precision MicroScaled GEMM. We then use our error analyses to construct an adaptive precision Cholesky factorization that exploits low-precision formats while respecting a prescribed element-wise error bound, as long as the factorization succeeds. We test it in two settings. First, we use it to choose the number of Ozaki 1 slices at each iteration, with SYRK/GEMM and TRSM emulated in INT8 fixed-point arithmetic to attain double-precision accuracy. Second, we use it to build a low-precision Cholesky preconditioner for the conjugate gradient method (PCG), in which SYRK/GEMM take low-precision inputs and accumulate in high precision, with the input format selected adaptively for each panel; if the factorization breaks down, diagonal perturbation still yields a valid preconditioner, at the cost of the error bound guarantees. On an NVIDIA GH200, the adaptive Ozaki 1-based factorization is up to 29% faster than a right-looking Cholesky using a fixed slice count of 7, and up to 69% faster than one using cuBLAS' Automatic Dynamic Precision (ADP), while maintaining the same error guarantees. For PCG, FP8 factorizations with diagonal perturbation form effective preconditioners on the 13 tested SuiteSparse matrices, reducing the number of PCG iterations by up to $12\times$ over CG on the same matrix diagonally scaled by powers of two. For synthetic matrices with arithmetic spectra, and geometric spectra with $κ\le 10^4$, FP8 preconditioners also reduce the number of CG iterations.

papers.title: Elicited Adaptation: Auditable Localized Fairness via Pairwise Queries
papers.abstract: How much must a predictor's scores change when a community's elicited fairness standard changes? Similarity and tolerance judgments define protected comparisons and acceptable score gaps. We study minimum uniform score movement on a fixed pool of $n$ profiles. For scores satisfying a source standard, we characterize the exact cost of retaining that standard during adaptation: runs of consecutive target constraints along shortest paths determine the optimal amplification factor. Its sharp worst case is $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$, and a full cost curve describes finite target-only repair budgets. Committing before the target is known can cost $n-1$ times the worst repair after revelation, even within one fixed convex ball of two-dimensional Mahalanobis metrics. Positive edge-budget floors cap both factors; bounded geometry also limits the commitment cost. At two interior targets of the construction attaining the $n-1$ bound, similarity queries alone yield a feasible $2$-approximate repair for tolerance $\eps\le1/[2(n-1)]$, reducing movement relative to common repair by a factor linear in $n$. Feasible $(1+α)$-optimal repair on this family has worst-case tolerance-query complexity $Θ(α^{-2}n^2\log(1/δ))$ under a fixed-slope logistic model. The analysis separates the information needed for a substantial adaptation benefit from the precision needed for nearly optimal movement. Elicitation studies and training comparisons examine tolerance choice and the relation between numerical compliance and predictive utility.

papers.title: A Five-Dimensional Geometric Formulation of Geophysical Fluid Dynamics
papers.abstract: We apply a geometric formulation of Newtonian dynamics to inviscid compressible geophysical flow, with gravity and the effects of rotating or moving coordinates incorporated in the metric tensor. This construction relies on the introduction of an auxiliary fifth coordinate, which allows mass and momentum transport, internal energy, and pressure work to be combined into a single mass--momentum tensor. The covariant divergence of this tensor leads to the continuity equation for mass density, the three momentum equations, and the thermodynamic equation, with the system closed by an equation of state. A time-independent metric also yields conservation of total energy. We recover familiar forms of the equations and illustrate the construction in rotating spherical and terrain-following coordinates. The thin-shell and spherical-geopotential approximations, with constant effective gravity, simplify the metric while retaining vertical gravity and the traditional Coriolis terms. Emphasis is placed on the connection between the geometric structure of the formulation and the equations commonly used in atmospheric dynamics.

papers.title: Early Readability of Trajectory Quality in Diffusion Driving Planners
papers.abstract: Diffusion-based driving planners can generate multiple trajectories for the same scene, but these candidates vary in quality. Can their internal states reveal which candidate will be better before denoising is complete? We systematically study this question in three pretrained planners: Alpamayo, ReCogDrive-IL, and HDP, using linear probes to predict final trajectory quality from intermediate states and evaluating candidate ranking and selection on held-out scenes. Across all three planners, we observe that states from the first denoiser evaluation already support informative selection, while further denoising does not consistently improve selection quality. Further analyses show that readout depends on the representation and reader, and that selection can coexist with limited overall ranking accuracy. These findings motivate an early-selection method that selects after the first denoiser evaluation and completes only the chosen candidate. This reduces computation relative to fully denoising every candidate and improves open-loop trajectory quality over random selection across all three planners. In particular, it reduces Alpamayo's average displacement error by 17.8% and 13.4% in one- and four-camera configurations, respectively. Closed-loop evaluations also show higher mean driving scores and progress.

papers.title: Inequality-Constrained Optimization via Sliding Mode Control
papers.abstract: We present COSMIC (Constrained Optimization via Sliding Mode for Inequality Constraints), a continuous-time solver for inequality-constrained optimization. COSMIC couples primal gradient-flow dynamics with multiplier dynamics derived from sliding mode control laws on a manifold defined by the smoothed Fischer-Burmeister function. We prove that COSMIC's trajectories reach this manifold in finite time from any primal initial point, after which the dynamics reduces to the gradient flow of a logarithmic barrier function. This yields a control-theoretic interpretation of barrier methods while allowing infeasible initialization. For strongly convex problems, we further establish exponential convergence to the minimizer. To address the numerical stiffness that arises in discretization, we develop a modified discrete-time algorithm. We validate COSMIC across various machine learning applications, demonstrating its ability to solve optimization problems accurately while scaling effectively to high-dimensional settings.

papers.title: Dymnikova black string
papers.abstract: We obtain a new static black string solution of Einstein's equations with a negative cosmological constant sourced by a Dymnikova-type anisotropic matter distribution. At large radial distances, the geometry approaches the Lemos black string, while the behavior near the central region is characterized by an effective curvature parameter. We examine the weak and strong energy conditions, the horizon structure, and the curvature invariants. The Ricci and Kretschmann scalars remain finite at the origin. We also investigate the Hawking temperature and heat capacity, with particular attention to the dependence of the thermodynamic behavior on the Dymnikova scale.

papers.title: RIFT: Reward Improvement Field Transfer for Cross-Domain Offline RL
papers.abstract: Learning from limited target data is a central challenge in cross-domain offline reinforcement learning. Abundant source data can help, but dynamics differences can make direct transition reuse unreliable. We propose Reward Improvement Field Transfer (RIFT), which instead learns how low- and high-reward source transitions differ. RIFT encodes source and target transitions in a shared latent space, pairs low- and high-reward source transitions using optimal transport, and fits an affine field to their displacements. It applies this field to low-reward target anchors and decodes the results to augment the target dataset. The approach builds on the hypothesis that related domains can share useful low-to-high reward structure despite different dynamics. We bound synthesis error under shared class geometry, identify conditions favoring target anchoring over source-high transplant, and derive a conditional connection to downstream return. Experiments on dense-reward locomotion tasks under gravity, morphology, and friction shifts show improved aggregate performance over existing baselines.

papers.title: Attacker Diversity Reduction in Adaptive LLM Red Teaming
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning can make automated red-teaming more successful while narrowing the attacks it produces. Co-training an attacker and a defender with group-relative policy optimization (GRPO) has been reported to reduce attacker diversity. This experiment reproduces attack diversity reduction using three runs with a Qwen2.5-14B attacker and a Phi-4-mini defender trained by direct preference optimization (DPO). The attacker receives a success-only reward and uses a length-unbiased loss, bounded updates, warm-up and ratio clipping. The attacker is evaluated on 26 AdvBench behaviors. Training ended after 12 rounds, following a decision based on development checkpoints, so the reported intervals are nominal. Attack Diversity Retention (ADR) compares the within-behavior of the trained attacker spread with the untrained attacker. In order for an attack diversity to be consider as having been reduced, a criterion requires the ADR to be below a 0.75 target with a 95% confidence interval together with continued attacker effectiveness. Therefore, if an attacker narrows its attack vector by 25% consistently its considered less diverse. After 24 attacker and 12 defender LORA-based updates, ADR for the three runs were 0.63, 0.61 and 0.63, respectively. Each run met the criterion at round 12; the earlier checks at rounds 4 and 8 fell short. Despite attacks being less diverse, attack success continued to improve as the attacker was updated after each training run.

papers.title: A discontinuous time to collision feedback: well posedness, regularity of the collision-time map, and residual stability of its Hamilton Jacobi approximations
papers.abstract: We analyze a finite-horizon time-to-collision map generated by an optimal-velocity prediction with bounded measurable leader acceleration and a feedback law that uses this map. The prediction describes nominal motion without the additional collision-avoidance feedback. Its first-contact geometry can produce discontinuities of the capped collision time at grazing, so smooth-feedback theory does not apply globally. For a prescribed leader--follower pair, we prove existence of Filippov solutions and exclusion of contact with negative relative velocity for every solution; a zero-speed touch is not excluded. Under explicit nondegeneracy hypotheses, trajectories cross the grazing set and uniqueness persists through the crossing. On the domain of transversal first contacts, the collision-time map is locally Lipschitz, continuously differentiable in the state, and differentiable in time outside a common null set. We quantify its sensitivity to the transversality margin and to jumps of the forcing. Characteristic and coarea arguments give boundary-plus-interior residual estimates for Hamilton--Jacobi approximations. An endpoint/age change of variables yields a stability coefficient controlled by flight time and terminal normal velocity, without inverse-transversality blowup. The estimates imply convergence conditional on vanishing continuum loss and pointwise identification under the stated trace and regularity assumptions. Numerical experiments on thirteen prescribed forcing profiles investigate boundary-error transport, sampling effects, and regularity predictions; a separate first-contact experiment numerically demonstrates post-threshold sensitivity sign changes. The guarantees concern the exact feedback and value-function approximation. Learned-feedback safety and convergence of a training algorithm remain open.

papers.title: $\ell^p$-Busemann space and the coarse Novikov conjecture
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of an \(\ell^p\)-Busemann space, which is a complete Busemann convex geodesic metric space whose tangent cones admit uniformly controlled homogeneous bi-Lipschitz embeddings into \(\ell^p\)-spaces. An \(\ell^p\)-Busemann space is called admissible if it contains dense sequences of closed convex subsets isometric to certain Finsler manifolds. We then prove that the rational coarse Novikov conjecture holds for proper metric spaces with bounded geometry that admit coarse embeddings into admissible \(\ell^p\)-Busemann spaces.

papers.title: Maximal dissipativity for the Dirichlet operator associated to the dynamical $Φ^4$ model on the plane
papers.abstract: We consider the Dirichlet/Kolmogorov operator associated with the stochastic quantization of the $Φ^4$ model on the plane whose domain is restricted to the space of smooth cylindrical functions. We prove that its closure is maximally dissipative in $L^p$. Our result implies the so-called $L^p$-uniqueness of the Dirichlet operator for every $1\le p<\infty$. In particular, essential self-adjointness and Markov uniqueness follow. The key ingredient is an estimate for the linearized equation for the dynamical $Φ^4_2$ model. The proof is based on techniques from singular SPDE theory and the stopping time argument introduced by Kunick and Tsatsoulis.

papers.title: Score-Based Stochastic Closure Modeling via Offline Indirect Learning and Online Data Assimilation
papers.abstract: Stochastic closure modeling is an emerging area in reduced-order modeling of large and complex (e.g., multiscale, multi-physics) systems, for which the computationally affordable reduced-order physical descriptions (e.g., digital twins for additive manufacturing, world models for AI agents) in numerical simulations inevitably lead to information losses that cannot be well addressed by classical deterministic closures. However, learning stochastic closures typically requires closure data that are difficult to obtain from measurements or often prohibitively expensive to compute using first-principles simulations. In this work, we develop a stochastic closure modeling framework that builds on score-based diffusion models, leveraging indirect offline training and online data assimilation without requiring the direct data of closures. Numerical experiments on two-dimensional turbulent flows demonstrate that indirect offline learning captures key closure statistics and improves predictions of system state. In addition, combining the learned closure with known physical dynamics leads to better generalization capability across different regimes than purely data-driven models that directly predict system state. Compared to standard data assimilation methods with a Gaussian assumption, the posterior-score assimilation better represents non-Gaussian features of the learned closure, and its combination with state-level data assimilation further improves prediction of the system state. The proposed framework enables stochastic closure modeling in realistic and challenging scenarios of complex dynamical systems in mechanics and engineering problems, where non-Gaussian statistics of model-form uncertainties are non-negligible (e.g., due to the nonlinearities of the system dynamics and/or the observations) and true closure data are not available, for both offline learning and online assimilation.

papers.title: Equivariant homomorphisms and Mordell--Weil groups of twists of Albanese varieties of cyclic multiple planes
papers.abstract: Let $X'\to X$ be a Galois cover of smooth projective varieties over a field $k$ with group $G$, and let $G$ act on an abelian variety $A$ over $k$. We prove an exact sequence relating the Mordell--Weil group of the twist of $A$ by $k(X')/k(X)$ to the group of $G$-equivariant homomorphisms from the Albanese variety of $X'$ to $A$; the remaining obstruction is killed by $|G|$. This corrects structure theorems in two earlier papers of the author and in a corrigendum to the first, where the equivariance condition was omitted. For the twists of Albanese varieties of cyclic multiple planes considered in those papers, we determine the rank and the torsion subgroup. Over number fields we describe the rank through the Galois action on endomorphisms and prove a specialization result. When $F(x,y)=0$ is the dual of the Fermat cubic, the Mordell curves $y^2=x^3+16F(a,b)$ have rank at least $3$ over $\mathbb Q$ for all $(a,b)\in {\mathbb Q}^2$ outside a thin set.

papers.title: Entanglement and Charge Transfer
papers.abstract: We compute the entropic order parameter introduced in (1905.10487) using the replica trick for two disjoint intervals. For a global symmetry, this quantity measures the mutual information carried by charge-anticharge intertwiners. We formulate the problem in terms of averages over twisted partition functions on replica Riemann surfaces, and obtain exact solutions for free fermions and compact bosons, for $U(1)$ symmetry and its discrete $\mathbb Z_N$ subgroups. We show that further averaging over both families of non-contractible cycles gives access to an additional quantity, which is the loss of Holevo information associated with complementary-charge measurements that occurs upon removing the intertwiners. For the boson, this quantity vanishes, whereas for Dirac fermions it equals the difference between the mutual information of the fermion-parity-gauged and ungauged theories, independently of the choice of even $\mathbb Z_N$ subgroup. Finally, we extend the analysis to non-Abelian symmetries using saddle expansions, deriving universal behavior in the nearly touching intervals limit and for a large number of fermions $N_F\gg1$.

papers.title: A dual-moment phenomenological framework for gravitational,electromagnetic and strong interactions
papers.abstract: The unification of fundamental interactions remains an outstanding open problem in fundamental physics. Most existing unification schemes rely on extra dimensions, exotic symmetries, or unobserved dynamical degrees of freedom. Here we construct a minimal classical phenomenological framework built on primitive charges and motion-induced kinetic dual moments. Gravitational, electromagnetic, and strong interactions are coherently formulated within a unified inverse-square-law structure. We postulate a universal coupling relation connecting source-charge couplings and moment-mediated couplings across these interaction sectors. Although weak-charge degrees of freedom can be formally accommodated within the formalism, full quantitative treatment of weak-interaction dynamics is left for future work. The model recovers well-established low-energy limits for planetary orbits, atomic systems, and heavy-quark hadrons. Importantly, it yields distinguishable corrections to light deflection by rapidly spinning compact objects, and three independent experimental schemes are proposed to test these predictions.

papers.title: Thermodynamics of Kerr-Newman-Bertotti-Robinson black holes from background subtraction
papers.abstract: The non-asymptotic flatness of the charged rotating black holes immersed in the Bertotti-Robinson magnetic field causes the ambiguity in the gauge choice for the time generator and the electric potential. By using the newly established form of the integrability condition together with the gauge choice for the asymptotically flat charged rotating black holes as the initial condition, we have found that the gauge can be uniquely fixed. With this fixed gauge, we further obtain the mass and angular momentum by the background subtraction method with the Minkowski spacetime as the reference spacetime. As a result, not only is the first law of black hole thermodynamics as well as the quantum statistical relation automatically satisfied, but also both the Christodoulou-Ruffini relation and the Smarr formula are obeyed.

papers.title: The Outer Eshelby Problem in Amorphous Solids with Odd Dipole Screening
papers.abstract: The so-called "2-dimensional Eshelby problem" was defined by JD Eshelby, where a circle is cut out of an elastic sheet, deformed into an ellipse, and forced back into the material. This creates a quadrupolar response which turned out to be very relevant for describing plastic deformations in amorphous solids. Moreover, the resulting strain field has been used to describe how elasto-plastic models respond to external strains. It is thus important to examine carefully the Eshelby problem in amorphous solids, especially when anomalous elasticity is at play. Here we solve the Eshelby problem in amorphous solids with both even and odd dipole screening and a complete analytical result is obtained for the displacement and strain fields. The analytical results are crucial for understanding the anomalous responses in displacement fields measured directly from experiments and numerical simulations. The computation of strain fields clearly demonstrates the deviations from their classical counterparts for perfectly elastic solids. The decomposition of the displacement field shows the excitation of higher-order Fourier modes. The presence of higher excitations other than the imposed Eshelby geometry therefore suggests the possible nonlinear mode coupling that can influence and modify the anomalous responses.

papers.title: Strong convergence rates for numerical approximations of the stochastic Burgers equation with additive rough noise
papers.abstract: We establish strong convergence rates for a fully discrete approximation of the one-dimensional stochastic Burgers equation driven by additive rough noise $(-A)^αdW$, $0\leα<1/4$, below the critical roughness threshold $α=1/4$. Through the Cole--Hopf transformation, the nonlinear equation is converted into a linear stochastic heat equation with spatially correlated multiplicative noise, which is discretized by a spectral Galerkin method in space and an accelerated exponential Euler method in time. A numerical approximation of the original solution is then reconstructed through a scale-invariant regularized inverse Cole--Hopf transformation. The convergence analysis combines strong Sobolev error estimates with strict positivity and uniform inverse-moment bounds for the exact transformed solution. Under an initial approximation condition and a weak-$L^4$ tail assumption on the transformed initial datum, we obtain the spatial strong convergence rates arbitrarily close to $1/2-2α$ and a temporal rate of order $1/2$, up to a logarithmic correction.
