Existing error-detection methods produce heuristic or uncalibrated scores, providing no formal control over missed errors and no principled way to trade off safety against clinician review burden. We introduce Conformal Assessment for Risk Evaluation (CARE), a post-hoc risk-control layer that adds calibrated omission and hallucination annotations without retraining the summarizer. CARE uses scalar conformal risk control (CRC) to bound the probability that a document contains an unflagged hallucinated sentence, and Learn-Then-Test fixed-sequence testing (LTT-FST) to control the expected fraction of true omissions left unsurfaced for review. Omission surfacing depends jointly on sentence importance and summary coverage, a two-dimensional threshold-selection problem; we show that calibrating one gate and then imposing an uncalibrated second gate can invalidate risk control. Across five medical summarization tasks, mean held-out violation over 100 random calibration/test resplits remains at or below the target for both controllers. At $α=0.15$, LTT-FST achieves the lowest review workload on three of five datasets among omission baselines held to the same confidence guarantee. Review workload varies by task and is highest for long, high-compression documents. On 46 clinician-annotated documents, the calibrated hallucination controller flags 88% of clinician-identified hallucinated sentences. In a preliminary study of 75 clinician reviews, assisted review-time omission coverage increased from 50.4% to 79.0% without increasing review time. Overall, CARE provides a principled framework for targeted, risk-controlled review of LLM-generated medical summaries.

papers.title: New Codes from Cyclic and Negacyclic Codes of Even Length over $\mathbb{Z}_4$
papers.abstract: This paper uses theoretical results previously established in the literature to design search algorithms to find new linear codes over $\mathbb{Z}_4$ from cyclic and negacyclic codes of even length. As a result of these searches, we have found 2500 new cyclic codes and 730 negacyclic codes. These new codes exhibit improved parameters compared to previously known codes. Additionally, we have obtained binary quantum codes with good parameters from such $\mathbb{Z}_4$ codes.

papers.title: Numerical Analysis of the Finite Transposition Method for Backward Stochastic Differential Equations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a finite transposition method for the numerical approximation of backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs). Starting from the transposition formulation of BSDEs, we construct appropriate finite-dimensional transposition spaces and establish the existence and uniqueness of the corresponding finite transposition solutions. We prove the convergence of the proposed method under standard assumptions and derive convergence rates under additional Malliavin regularity assumptions. The proposed approach provides a variational approximation framework for BSDEs and may be viewed as a stochastic counterpart of the classical finite element method for partial differential equations. In addition, the conditional expectations arising in the resulting scheme can be evaluated explicitly, thereby facilitating its numerical implementation.

papers.title: A Spherical Stochastic Geometry Framework for Patrol-Based HAPs Network: Coverage and Energy Efficiency Analysis
papers.abstract: This paper develops a stochastic geometry framework for high-altitude platform station (HAP) networks in which platforms execute cyclic patrol trajectories anchored to designated service regions. We introduce two small-circle ring point-process models on the spherical Earth. In the small-circle ring Poisson Cox process (SCR-PCP), platforms form one-dimensional Poisson point processes on localized patrol rings, whereas in the small-circle ring binomial cluster process (SCR-BCP), each ring contains a fixed number of uniformly distributed platforms. We establish the isotropy of both models and derive spatial statistics, including the distributions of the nearest-anchor, nearest-ring, and nearest-HAP distances, together with the serving-ring angle distribution. Building on these results, we derive coverage probability expressions under nearest-visible-HAP association by decomposing aggregate interference into same-ring and other-ring components and characterizing their conditional Laplace transforms. To account for the flight dynamics of patrol-based HAPs, we integrate a steady circular flight propulsion model with the communication analysis and introduce a coverage energy efficiency (CEE) metric. This yields a necessary optimality condition for an interior energy-optimal patrol radius that balances coverage performance against the propulsion cost of circular flight. Numerical results reveal fundamental differences between intensity-driven (SCR-PCP) and finite-fleet (SCR-BCP) deployments and demonstrate that patrol geometry, platform density, and cruising velocity should be jointly considered to achieve energy-efficient HAP operation.

papers.title: CausalPOI: Spatio-Temporal Graph-Based Causal Modeling for Cold-Start POI Check-in Forecasting
papers.abstract: As urban environments continue to evolve rapidly, accurately modeling the dynamic behaviour of Points of Interest is essential for supporting data-driven urban planning and commercial decision-making. While recent advancements in spatio-temporal graph learning have improved POI forecasting, most methods rely on proximity-based graphs and correlation-driven modeling, which overlook the functional dependencies between POIs and fail to capture the causal effects of urban interventions. In this paper, we introduce a novel research problem -- cold-start POI check-in forecasting, which aims to predict the future check-in pattern of a newly introduced POI, by modeling its temporal evolution and functional interactions with nearby POIs in a structured urban spatial context. To address these challenges, we propose CausalPOI, a spatio-temporal graph-based causal representation learning framework. CausalPOI leverages Spatio-Temporal Functional Interaction Graph to model semantic and spatial relationships between POIs, and constructs structurally aligned treatment and control graphs to simulate factual and counterfactual scenarios. Extensive experiments on real-world SafeGraph datasets demonstrate that CausalPOI significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across the board, validating its effectiveness in spatio-temporal forecasting, semantic interaction modeling, and causal effect estimation, providing a more interpretable and actionable foundation for urban intervention analysis. Source code is available at Github.

papers.title: An Octahedral Fibrous Constitutive Model for Heart Valve Mechanics and Function
papers.abstract: Fibrous soft tissues derive their nonlinear mechanical response from networks of extracellular matrix fibers. The organization of fibers and their load-bearing characteristics give rise to strain stiffening, the reverse Poynting effect, and anisotropic mechanical behavior. Motivated by these coupled features, we develop an anisotropic hyperelastic model for fibrous biological tissues that accounts for the contribution of the fiber network under both tensile and compressive deformation in an asymmetric fashion. The model uses an octahedral arrangement of fibers embedded in a ground matrix, allowing anisotropy, fiber volume fraction, and pre-stretch to influence the material response. We calibrate the model to experimental data for mitral valve leaflets using an inverse finite element approach that is coupled to automatic differentiation to facilitate efficient parameter calibration. The calibrated model reproduces responses across biaxial, pure-shear, and constrained-uniaxial tests, while separate numerical tests demonstrate its ability to represent substantial volume reduction and the reverse Poynting effect. Using the calibrated model, we investigate how anisotropy and fiber reorientation affect valve deformation under physiological loading. In the idealized valve, the reference fiber orientation, which provided greater radial compliance, yielded complete leaflet coaptation. Prescribed local fiber reorientation redistributed leaflet stress but did not compromise coaptation. Swapping the preferred material directions throughout the leaflets, by contrast, prevented closure in the simulated valve. Finally, we examine how fiber pre-stretch and collagen volume fraction affect leaflet strain and contact, finding a stronger response to changes in pre-stretch over the parameter ranges studied.

papers.title: Is Agentic AI Ready for Real-World Hardware Engineering? A Deep Dive with Phoenix-bench
papers.abstract: We ask whether agentic AI systems built for software engineering transfer to realistic hardware engineering. Existing hardware LLM benchmarks isolate sub-tasks but none jointly requires repository navigation, hierarchy-aware localization, Electronic Design Automation (EDA) executable verification, and maintenance-style patching. We introduce \textbf{Phoenix-bench}, a synchronized corpus of 511 verified Verilator instances from 114 GitHub repositories, each shipped with the developer patch, design-flow labels, fail-to-pass and pass-to-pass testbenches, and a Docker-pinned EDA environment so resolved-rate differences reflect agent behavior rather than toolchain availability. Using Phoenix-bench we run a uniform evaluation of four commercial agents and eight open-source agentic structures across four LLM backbones, plus two diagnostic interventions (file-level oracle localization and one round of testbench-log feedback). Three findings emerge. (i)~Software and hardware are fundamentally different engineering tasks: the same agent loses 37\% to 58\% from SWE-bench Verified to Phoenix-bench because hardware bugs propagate across parallel instantiated modules through signal flow rather than along a software-style call graph, and software-tuned agents stop at the symptom file instead of tracing back through the instantiation chain. (ii)~Failures concentrate on design control-flow / finite state machine (FSM) bugs, verification testbench bugs, and hard cases that demand cross-hierarchy signal-flow tracking and coordinated multi-file edits. (iii)~Localization granularity matters far more than localization itself: a perfect file-level oracle yields only $+1.4$\% because the agent then breaks files that did not need editing, while a single round of test case feedback lifts resolved rate by $42$\% to $45$\% because the test case tells \emph{where} the bug is and \emph{what} the fix has to look like.

papers.title: Monomial bases and canonical bases for quantum affine algebras
papers.abstract: We construct a monomial basis of a quantum affine algebra of simply-laced type, associated to the PBW basis of Beck-Nakajima. We show that there exists a simple algorithm of computing canonical basis in terms of the monomial basis. We dsicuss the relations of the canonical basis obtained from this PBW basis with Lusztig's canonical basis constructed by using the geometry of quivers.

papers.title: Reward-Weighted On-Policy Distillation with an Open Property-Equivalence Verifier for NL-to-SVA Generation
papers.abstract: Specialized language models for translating natural language (NL) into SystemVerilog assertions (SVA) reach approximately 76\% accuracy on NL2SVA-Human, but aggregate scores obscure errors on bounded-delay and liveness specifications. Models often reuse a small set of implication templates where different temporal behavior is required. Supervised fine-tuning rewards agreement with reference tokens, whereas SVA correctness depends on property equivalence. We propose \emph{reward-weighted on-policy distillation} (RWOPD), which uses an open SymbiYosys+Z3 property-equivalence checker to select student rollouts and weight their distillation loss. A frozen 14B teacher supplies forward Kullback--Leibler (KL) supervision at each response token; equivalent rollouts receive greater weight than one-sided implications. Starting from curriculum supervised fine-tuning (SFT), RWOPD distills CodeV-SVA-14B into a Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct student. The student has the highest reported pass@1, pass@5, and pass@10 on NL2SVA-Human and NL2SVA-Machine among the compared models, including specialized baselines and 671B general-purpose models.

papers.title: Discrete Flow Matching for Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Many reinforcement learning (RL) tasks have discrete action spaces, but most generative policy methods based on diffusion and flow matching are designed for continuous control. Meanwhile, generative policies usually rely heavily on offline datasets and offline-to online RL is itself challenging, as the policy must improve from new interaction without losing useful behavior learned from static data. To address those challenges, we introduce DRIFT, an online fine-tuning method that updates an offline pretrained continuous time Markov chain (CTMC) policy with an advantage-weighted discrete flow matching loss. To preserve useful pretrained knowledge, we add a path-space penalty that regularizes the full CTMC trajectory distribution, rather than only the final action distribution. For large discrete action spaces, we introduce a candidate-set approximation that updates the actor over a small subset of actions sampled from reference-policy rollouts and uniform exploration. Our theoretical analysis shows that focusing on a small set of high probability actions can reduce computation while keeping the approximation error small, making our method practical for large action spaces. We evaluate on macro-action MinAtar games where offline-pretrained DRIFT outperforms its online-only counterpart across all five games and achieves the highest mean return on three and on oracle free Jericho, DRIFT achieves a mean normalized score of 7.3\% with a lightweight GRU encoder, outperforming the evaluated pretrained language-model baselines. Ablations demonstrate the importance of appropriately weighted path-space regularization and reference-guided candidate construction.

papers.title: Reflection Anchors for Propagation-Aware Visual Retention in Long-Chain Multimodal Reasoning
papers.abstract: Long chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning improves large vision--language models, but visual information often fades during generation, limiting long-horizon multimodal reasoning. Existing methods either re-inject vision at inference or train policies for stronger grounding, but where to intervene relies on perception heuristics rather than principled gain analysis, and how local visual influence propagates remains implicit. We study this problem from an information-theoretic standpoint and derive a lower bound on the downstream visual gain of a one-step intervention, which suggests two factors: local branching room (token entropy) and downstream visual propagation potential (suffix divergence from a vision-marginalized reference). Guided by this analysis, we propose reflection-anchor policy optimization (RAPO), a GRPO-based policy optimization method that selects high-entropy reflection anchors and optimizes a chain-masked finite-window KL surrogate for downstream visual dependence. Experiments on reasoning-intensive and general-domain benchmarks show that RAPO delivers substantial gains over strong baselines across multiple LVLM backbones. Mechanism analyses further indicate that reflection anchors are enriched for visually sensitive decision points and that RAPO increases contrastive visual-dependence signals along generated trajectories.

papers.title: Nonparametric estimation of time-varying network connections by multi-stage smoothing
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of estimating the underlying edge probabilities of a time-varying network observed at multiple time points. The probability structure is represented by a time-varying graphon that satisfies temporal Hölder smoothness and piecewise Lipschitz conditions in the latent variables. We propose a multi-stage smoothing estimator that first applies temporal local smoothing to each edge and then performs node-domain smoothing using a data-driven neighborhood construction adapted from the method. An additional temporal smoothing step is introduced as an optional refinement when uniform accuracy over the entire time domain is required. Simulation studies demonstrate the benefits of combining temporal and node-domain smoothing under different generative models. We also apply the method to a real time-varying network dataset and show that it captures both smooth temporal evolution and structural patterns in the connectivity.

papers.title: Joint Consistency: A Unified Test-Time Aggregation Framework via Energy Minimization
papers.abstract: This paper studies test-time aggregation, an approach that generates multiple reasoning traces and aggregates them into a final answer. Most existing methods rely on evaluation signals collected from candidate traces in isolation or answer frequencies, while ignoring comparative interactions among candidates. We propose Joint Consistency (JC), formulated as a constrained Ising-type energy minimization problem, which employs both independent evaluation signals and pairwise comparisons using LLM-as-a-judge. JC provides a unified framework for test-time aggregation that subsumes typical voting and weighted aggregation methods as special cases. Moreover, we develop an efficient approximation strategy that makes interaction modeling practical for large-scale test-time aggregation. Experiments on math and code reasoning benchmarks show that JC outperforms existing baselines across tasks, judge models, trace budgets, and trace-generation settings, with particularly pronounced gains on challenging problems.

papers.title: Exact SU(2) Yang-Mills Waves from a Simple Ansatz
papers.abstract: We use an ansatz based on rotations of the Pauli basis to construct exact propagating solutions of the sourceless SU(2) Yang--Mills equations in $(3+1)$ dimensions. By examining and extending this ansatz, we obtain two wave families with nontrivial transverse structures and a family of finite-amplitude waves on a self-similar non-Abelian background. These solutions can retain a genuinely non-Abelian structure while admitting arbitrary wave profiles propagating at the speed of light and carrying the corresponding longitudinal electric or magnetic fields. We also investigate the parameter conditions for their non-Abelian character and their energy transport. For the self-similar family, we study the structure of its singular plane and construct suitable sources to replace the singular region while preserving wave propagation in the remaining regions. This offers a possible interpretation of these solutions as propagating fields outside sources.

papers.title: AAC: Admissible-by-Architecture Differentiable Landmark Compression for ALT
papers.abstract: We introduce the Architecturally Admissible Compressor (AAC), which adapts landmark-based A* heuristics to query demand under a fixed label-memory budget. AAC provides two continuous relaxations of ALT (A*, Landmarks, and Triangle inequality) selection. With exact landmark distances, every parameter value defines a lower bound on shortest-path distance. Both relaxations deploy ALT using only the selected labels. The row-stochastic relaxation takes convex combinations of landmark distances. We characterize the maximal admissibility-preserving linear classes and prove that the relaxed and discrete optima coincide. The fractional relaxation mixes subset heuristics and supports continuous greedy (AAC-CG) with exact gradients and an entropy-regularized oracle for differentiable selection. For expected heuristic value, we prove an approximation guarantee with finite-step, oracle-error, and finite-sample terms. The limiting $1-1/e$ factor is optimal for arbitrary supplied pools and query distributions unless P${=}$NP. At matched label memory, AAC-CG reduces A* expansions by $1.9$-$22.7$% relative to farthest-point ALT (FPS-ALT) in all $19$ tested combinations of graph and memory budget across six road networks and two synthetic graphs. Each combination uses one $500$-query test split; all methods share distance tables when distances are symmetric. Canonical greedy also expands fewer nodes than FPS-ALT in all $19$ graph-budget pairs. AAC-CG achieves $99.6$% of canonical greedy's mean heuristic value on test queries, averaged over these pairs. AAC makes admissibility independent of training success, while its analysis and experiments distinguish selection quality from search efficiency.

papers.title: Appear2Meaning: A Cross-Cultural Benchmark for Structured Cultural Metadata Inference from Images
papers.abstract: Museum records express how people understand heritage objects through cultural and historical relations. Recovering these human attributions from images is a technical challenge for vision-language models (VLMs). We introduce Appear2Meaning, a cross-cultural benchmark of 750 museum objects for image-only recovery of title, culture, period, origin, and creator. Its evaluation framework distinguishes field-level from complete-record compatibility and uses human validation for semantic judgement. Across nine VLMs, mean field accuracy is 36.16--49.82%; 7.20--17.02% of records have all four contextual fields compatible, and 2.13--7.87% have all five, including title. For the two tested models, image-only input yields 12.6--32.2 percentage points higher reference compatibility for culture, period, and origin than a museum-and-title-only control.

papers.title: Not All Turns Are Equally Hard: Adaptive Thinking Budgets For Efficient Multi-Turn Reasoning in Agents
papers.abstract: As LLM reasoning performance plateaus, improving inference-time compute efficiency is crucial to mitigate overthinking and long thinking traces even for simple queries. Prior approaches including length regularization, adaptive routing and difficulty-based budget allocation primarily focus on single-turn settings and fail to address the sequential dependencies inherent in multi-turn reasoning. We formulate multi-turn reasoning as a sequential compute allocation problem and model it as a multi-objective Markov Decision Process. We propose TAB: Turn-Adaptive Budgets, a budget allocation policy that takes as input the conversation history and learns to maximize task accuracy while respecting global per-problem token constraints, and consequently learns to adaptively allot smaller budgets to easier turns and save an appropriate number of tokens for the crucial harder reasoning steps. We train and analyze the behavior of TAB on an auxiliary hierarchical plan-and-execute system for multi-turn math reasoning where solution trajectories are inexpensive to collect. Here, TAB saves up to 35% tokens and 30% latency over static and off-the-shelf LLM budget baselines. We then transfer the same TAB policy to environment-grounded agentic workflows spanning sequential tool-use, simulated user-agent dialogue and multi-step terminal tasks, where it generalizes and maintains accuracy while saving up to 20% tokens and 15% latency, without ever being trained on them.

papers.title: Connection between the contextuality breaking and incompatibility breaking qubit channels
papers.abstract: Contextuality and measurement incompatibility are two fundamental aspects of nonclassicality, and their manifestations in observed quantum correlations are often deeply interconnected. Recently, measurement incompatibility has been studied in connection with nonlocality, particularly in terms of their robustness under various quantum channels. This line of investigation helps to establish a connection between the channels that break nonlocality and those that break incompatibility. In this study, we focus on an asymmetric bipartite Bell scenario involving three and four inputs on Alice's and Bob's sides, respectively, with each of these inputs having dichotomous outcomes. Under the assumption of locality, the observed statistics in this asymmetric scenario obey the elegant Bell inequality (EBI). Here, we use a different version of the EBI that relies on the assumption of preparation noncontextuality. By taking the violation of this noncontextual version of EBI as a witness of preparation contextuality we establish a connection between the channels that break contextuality and the channels that break triplewise measurement incompatibility. Our results suggest that any channel which breaks EBI contextuality will also break Clauser Horne Shimony Holt contextuality; however, the reverse does not hold. We also show that a depolarizing channel that breaks N wise incompatibility can also break a certain form of contextuality, witnessed by a generalized inequality involving N measurements on one wing of a bipartite Bell scenario.

papers.title: SARL: Label-Free Reinforcement Learning by Rewarding Reasoning Topology
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning is critical to improving large reasoning models, but its success relies heavily on verifiable rewards (RLVR), making it hard to use in open-ended domains where correctness is ambiguous and cannot be verified. Moreover, reasoning trajectories remain largely unconstrained, and optimizing solely toward the final answer can favor early exploitation over generalization. In this work, we ask whether general reasoning ability can be improved by teaching models how to think (the structure of reasoning) rather than what to produce (the outcome of reasoning), and we extend traditional RLVR to open-ended settings. We introduce Structure-Aware Reinforcement Learning (SARL), a label-free framework that constructs per-response reasoning maps from intermediate thinking steps and rewards their reasoning topology. SARL shifts supervision from destination to path, encouraging reasoning trajectories that are both locally coherent and globally efficient. On verifiable math tasks, SARL outperforms prior label-free RL baselines and even exceeds RL methods with ground truth supervision, with average gains of +9.1% under PPO and +11.6% under GRPO across four math benchmarks, with particularly large improvements on AIME25 (+35.5% with PPO and +44.7% with GRPO). On non-verifiable open-ended tasks, SARL achieves average gains of +34.6% under PPO and +30.4% under GRPO on WildBench across five task categories, outperforming prior label-free RL methods and DPO, which relies on additional preference labels. Beyond strong performance, SARL exhibits substantially lower KL divergence and higher policy entropy, indicating more stable and exploratory training dynamics. Code and data are available at \href{https://github.com/cacayaya/SARL}{Code Link}.

papers.title: Interfacial Resistance and Preferential Internal Mixing of Phase-Separated Condensates
papers.abstract: Biomolecular condensates spatially organize biochemical processes. They can selectively partition molecules and enrich them well above their concentration outside. Their function depends on the exchange of molecules with their surroundings, whose kinetics are determined not only by partitioning and diffusion but also by interfacial resistance. The latter can hinder molecules from crossing the condensate boundary, thereby increasing their residence times in the condensate and promoting repeated encounters with interaction partners therein. So far, it has proven difficult to measure the interfacial resistance of condensates experimentally. Here, we combine fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) with fluorescence correlation spectroscopy (FCS) and calibrated fluorescence imaging to disentangle partitioning, interfacial resistance, and differences in diffusion inside and outside of condensates. Applying this approach to polyelectrolyte condensates across a range of salt concentrations, we find substantial, salt-dependent interfacial resistance, which causes molecules to undergo multiple rounds of internal mixing before escaping. DDX4-YFP condensates in living cells also exhibit substantial interfacial resistance, although they are more permeable than polyelectrolyte condensates with comparable partition coefficients. Our results indicate that interfacial resistance is a tunable property of condensates that can place them in distinct transport regimes, favoring distinct functions such as dynamic reaction crucibles or insulated molecular sinks.

papers.title: Template-Driven Machine Learning Standardization for Large Model Fleets
papers.abstract: Modern computational advertising platforms typically rely on recommendation systems to predict user responses, such as click-through rates, conversion rates, and other optimization events. To support a wide variety of product surfaces and advertiser goals, these platforms maintain an extensive ecosystem of machine learning (ML) models. Operating at this scale, however, creates significant development and efficiency challenges: substantial engineering effort is required to regularly refresh these models and propagate new techniques, resulting in long latencies when deploying innovations across the ecosystem. We present a large-scale empirical study comparing model performance, efficiency, and technique propagation between a standardized model-building approach and independent per-model optimization in recommendation systems. To facilitate standardization, we propose the Standard Model Template (SMT)---a framework that generates high-performance models adaptable to diverse data distributions and optimization events. By composing standardized ML model components, SMT reduces technique-propagation complexity from $O(n \cdot k)$ to $O(n+k)$, where $n$ is the number of models and $k$ the number of techniques. Evaluating an extensive suite of models over five global development cycles within Meta's production ads ranking ecosystem, our launched results demonstrate: (1) a 0.77\% average improvement in cross-entropy at neutral serving capacity; (2) a 1.52\% cumulative online metric lift; (3) a 92\% reduction in per-model iteration engineering time; and (4) a 6.3$\times$ increase in technique--model pair adoption throughput. These findings challenge the conventional wisdom that diverse optimization goals inherently require diversified ML model design.

papers.title: Variational Trajectory Optimization of Anisotropic Diffusion Schedules
papers.abstract: We introduce a variational framework for diffusion models with anisotropic noise schedules parameterized by a matrix-valued path $M_t(θ)$ that allocates noise across subspaces. Central to our framework is a trajectory-level objective that jointly trains the score network and \emph{learns} $M_t(θ)$, which encompasses general parameterization classes of matrix-valued noise schedules. We further derive an estimator for $\partial_θ\nabla \log p_t$ that enables efficient optimization of the $M_t(θ)$ schedule. For inference, we develop an efficiently-implementable reverse-ODE solver that is an anisotropic generalization of the second-order Heun discretization algorithm. Across CIFAR-10, AFHQv2, FFHQ, and ImageNet-64, our method consistently improves FID with largest gains at low NFE. Code is available at https://github.com/kilonova801/anisotropic-diffusion.

papers.title: On the effective Yau--Tian--Donaldson conjecture for projective bundles
papers.abstract: Consider the projectivization $\mathbb{P}(E)$ of a holomorphic vector bundle $E$ over a smooth curve, equipped with a fixed Kähler class $[ω]$. Our first main result establishes that the existence of an extremal Kähler metric in $[ω]$ is equivalent to the weighted stability of a moment polytope $Δ$ with respect to explicit weight functions depending on the topological data of $\mathbb{P}(E)$. We then introduce a class of test configurations, which we call compatible test configurations. These are constructed by gluing horospherical test configurations of the fibers, arising from convex functions on $Δ$ via Delcroix's construction, to the principal bundle associated with $\mathbb{P}(E)$. Our second main result shows that the weighted stability of $Δ$ naturally arises when computing the relative uniform K-stability of $[ω]$ with respect to compatible test configurations.

papers.title: Equivariant Kazhdan--Lusztig Polynomials of Thagomizer Matroids with a Hyperoctahedral Group Action
papers.abstract: We compute the equivariant Kazhdan--Lusztig and inverse Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials of the thagomizer matroid $T_n=M(K_{1,1,n})$ under the action of the hyperoctahedral group $\Bn$. For $n\ge2$, this action identifies $\Bn$ with the full automorphism group of $T_n$. For every $n\ge0$, we give multiplicity-free decompositions of all coefficients of both polynomials into irreducible representations and prove that both coefficient sequences are strongly induced log-concave with respect to induction from $\Bn\times\Bn$ to $\B{2n}$. The formulas for Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials follow from the palindromicity of the equivariant $Z$-polynomial and the known equivariant formulas for the graphic matroids of cycle graphs under the action of $\Sn$. The inverse formula follows from Proudfoot's equivariant inversion identity. For $n\ge2$, we also obtain explicit formulas for both polynomials of $M(K_{2,n})$ under the inherited action of $\Bn$, again with multiplicity-free coefficients.

papers.title: USER: A Unified and Extensible System for Online Real-World Policy Learning in Embodied AI
papers.abstract: Online policy learning directly in the physical world is a promising yet challenging direction for embodied intelligence. Unlike simulation, real-world systems cannot be arbitrarily accelerated, cheaply reset, or massively replicated, suggesting that real-world policy learning is not merely an algorithmic problem, but inherently a systems problem. We present \user, a \underline{U}nified and extensible \underline{S}yst\underline{E}m for online real-world policy lea\underline{R}ning. On the systems side, \user introduces a hardware abstraction layer for unified robot management and an adaptive communication plane that enables efficient cloud-edge training. On the learning side, \user adopts a fully asynchronous training framework, designs a persistent and cache-aware replay buffer, and provides extensible abstractions for rewards, algorithms, and policies. Experiments in both simulation and the real world demonstrate that \user supports multi-robot coordination, heterogeneous manipulators, cloud-edge training with large models, and long-running asynchronous training. Together, these capabilities establish \user as a unified and extensible systems foundation for online real-world policy learning.

papers.title: Flow Matching for Offline Reinforcement Learning with Discrete Actions
papers.abstract: Generative policies based on diffusion models and flow matching have shown strong promise for offline reinforcement learning (RL), but their applicability remains largely confined to continuous action spaces. To address a broader range of offline RL settings, we extend flow matching to a general framework that supports discrete action spaces with multiple objectives. Specifically, we replace continuous flows with continuous-time Markov chains, trained using a Q-weighted flow matching objective. We then extend our design to multi-agent settings, mitigating the exponential growth of joint action spaces via a factorized conditional path. For an oracle single policy-improvement step from the behavior distribution, we theoretically show that, under idealized conditions, the Q-weighted objective recovers the KL-regularized Boltzmann policy. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method performs robustly across diverse settings and benchmarks, including high-dimensional control, multi-agent games, and dynamically changing preferences over multiple objectives, while achieving competitive performance and demonstrating advantages in multimodal decision-making and preference-conditioned policy representation. Our discrete framework can also be applied to continuous-control problems through action quantization, providing a flexible trade-off between representational complexity and performance.

papers.title: Multi-layer Cross-attention is Provably Optimal for Multi-modal In-context Learning
papers.abstract: Recent progress has rapidly advanced our understanding of the mechanisms underlying in-context learning in modern attention-based neural networks. However, existing results focus exclusively on unimodal data; in contrast, the theoretical underpinnings of in-context learning for multi-modal data remain poorly understood. We introduce a mathematically tractable framework for studying multi-modal learning and explore when transformer-like architectures can recover Bayes-optimal performance in-context. To model multi-modal problems, we assume the observed data arises from a latent factor model. Our first result comprises a negative take on expressibility: we prove that single-layer self-attention models fail to recover the Bayes-optimal predictor uniformly over the task distribution. To address this limitation, we introduce a novel, linearized cross-attention mechanism, which we study in the regime where both the number of cross-attention layers and the context length are large. We show that this cross-attention mechanism is provably Bayes optimal when optimized using gradient flow. Our results underscore the benefits of depth for in-context learning and establish the provable utility of cross-attention for multi-modal distributions.

papers.title: MHRC-Bench: A Multilingual Hardware Repository-Level Code Completion benchmark
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have achieved strong performance on code completion in general-purpose programming languages, but existing repository-level benchmarks focus almost exclusively on software code and largely overlook hardware description languages (HDLs). We present \textbf{MHRC-Bench}, consisting of \textbf{MHRC-Bench-Train} and \textbf{MHRC-Bench-Eval}, the first benchmark for multilingual hardware code completion at the repository level with functional evaluation. MHRC-Bench covers three major hardware design coding styles and annotates each completion target with code-structure-level and hardware-oriented semantic labels derived from concrete syntax tree (CST) analysis. Post-training billion-scale code LLMs on MHRC-Bench-Train enables smaller open-weight models to outperform much larger general-purpose models under matched context windows. Beyond aggregate accuracy, our analysis surfaces four findings that distinguish hardware from software code completion: \emph{(i)}~performance varies sharply across HDLs, with high-level synthesis (HLS) easiest and VHDL hardest in most settings across functional pass rate, exact match (EM), and edit similarity (ES); \emph{(ii)}~hardware accuracy is non-monotonic in code-structure depth, in contrast with the monotonic depth--accuracy curve known for software; \emph{(iii)}~accuracy plateaus once the input context exceeds 2{,}048 tokens, while software completion continues to benefit from longer context; and \emph{(iv)}~certain repository-level retrievers tuned on software underperform a no-retrieval baseline on HDL repositories because their structural and dependency assumptions are violated by hardware code.

papers.title: Full-Time-Scale Power Management for Hybrid AC/DC/DS Microgrid with Dynamic Concatenation and Global Equivalent Circuit Modeling
papers.abstract: Hybrid AC/DC/distributed energy storage (DS) microgrids (MGs) provide an effective solution for improving power accessibility and supply reliability in remote and isolated areas.Conventional static power management aims to proportionally allocate power based on unit ratings by scheduling the operation of interlinking converters (ILCs). Recent studies on transient power management emphasize inertia coupling among subgrids by dynamically regulating ILC power flows, thereby enhancing the system resilience against disturbances. In existing literature, these two objectives are normally addressed in a separate fashion and a unified scheme to simultaneously achieve them is rarely found. Furthermore, conventional static management neglects droop-induced frequency and voltage deviations which may seriously compromise the safe operation of sensitive loads. To address these limitations, in this paper, we proposes a full-timescale (FTS) power management for the hybrid MG is proposed.Autonomous frequency/voltage restoration controls are deployed in each subgrid to eliminate droop-induced frequency and voltage deviations, based on which a novel FTS dynamic concatenator is proposed to chain up the static power sharing and transient inertia sharing across different timescales. Moreover, a novel global equivalent circuit model (GECM) is presented to interpret the holistic hybrid system from electrical circuit perspective. Then the static and transient performance of the complex hybrid AC/DC/DS MG can be quantitatively characterized to facilitate easier engineering practices. In-house experiments validate that the proposed FTS dynamic concatenator ensures static power sharing and transient inertia sharing through the ILC in full timescales.

papers.title: A choice-based axiomatization of Nash equilibrium
papers.abstract: An axiomatization of Nash equilibrium is provided for games of complete information in normal form. The Nash equilibrium correspondence is shown to be the unique solution concept that satisfies four simple and intuitive axioms. Two axioms reflect a mild form of individual rationality: one states that any profile of dominant strategies in a game must be a solution, whereas the other says that any solution to a game should not depend on strictly dominated strategies. The remaining two axioms are adaptations to non-cooperative games of standard choice-theoretic axioms about contraction and expansion consistency.

papers.title: A General Theorem for Non-Simultaneous Hat Guessing Puzzles
papers.abstract: The prisoners and hats puzzle, or simply the hat puzzle, is a family of games in which a group of prisoners are each assigned a colored hat and are asked to guess the color of their own hat. Various versions of the puzzle arise depending on the number of prisoners, the number of possible hat colors, and the information available to them before and after the game begins. These puzzles are broadly classified according to whether the prisoners' declarations are made simultaneously or non-simultaneously. In this paper we present a general theorem concerning the existence of a winning strategy when the declarations are non-simultaneous. We also discuss the relationship between the construction of such strategies and the Axiom of Choice, as well as their connection to the simultaneous-declaration case.

papers.title: Pseudospin order of the Bogoliubov de Gennes Hamiltonian
papers.abstract: We investigate a two-dimensional superconducting system with a smoothly and periodically varying order parameter, which is modulated along one direction while remaining uniform in the perpendicular direction, leading to a spatially periodic superconducting phase. It is known that the phase of the order parameter determines the relative phaseof the quasiparticle components. Here we demonstrate that the latter becomes observable through the associated Bloch vector, which provides a topological invariant that links the Bloch vector to an integer winding number. The Bloch vector can be understood as the expectation value of the pseudospin, for which the physical manifestation of the winding number is a helical ordering. For the Bogoliubov-de Gennes Hamiltonian with an edge we have both plane-wave solutions describing bulk states and exponentially localized solutions that correspond to edge modes. The analytic bulk-edge connection is employed to identify the conditions under which the edge states emerge from the bulk spectrum. The pseudospin ordering rotates under the energy change of the edge modes but is energy-independent for the bulk modes, except for the opposite sign in the upper and the lower band. These results establish a direct connection between the spatial modulation of the order parameter, the topological structure of the Bloch vector, as well as the relation between the order parameter phase and the pseudospin orientation of the edge modes.

papers.title: Influence of Network Topology and Vaccination Strategies on HPV Dynamics: A Simulation Study Using the SeCoNet Growth Model
papers.abstract: This study examines how contact network topology influences the effectiveness of vaccination programs in the context of human papillomavirus (HPV) transmission. Using the SeCoNet sexual contact network growth model, we evaluate age based, ring based, and several centrality based vaccination strategies across the overall, male, and female cohorts, focusing on peak incidence, timing of peak prevalence, and cumulative incidence. The simulations show that degree, betweenness, and percolation centrality based strategies are generally the most effective, while ring vaccination achieves the greatest reduction in cumulative incidence among females. Network topology also plays a critical role: higher average degree reduces vaccination effectiveness, whereas higher power-law exponent, longer average shortest path length, and stronger clustering improve vaccination outcomes. The results highlight the importance of incorporating network structure into the design of HPV vaccination programs.

papers.title: Controllable Generative Trajectory Prediction via Weak Preference Alignment
papers.abstract: Deep generative models such as conditional variational autoencoders (CVAEs) have shown great promise for predicting trajectories of surrounding agents in autonomous vehicle planning. State-of-the-art models have achieved remarkable accuracy in such prediction tasks. Besides accuracy, diversity is also crucial for safe planning because human behaviors are inherently uncertain and multimodal. However, existing methods generally lack a scheme to generate controllably diverse trajectories, which is arguably more useful than randomly diversified trajectories, to the end of safe planning. To address this, we propose PrefCVAE, an augmented CVAE framework that uses weakly labeled preference pairs to imbue latent variables with semantic attributes. Using average velocity as an example attribute, we demonstrate that PrefCVAE enables controllable, semantically meaningful predictions without degrading baseline accuracy. Our results show the effectiveness of preference supervision as a cost-effective way to enhance sampling-based generative models.

papers.title: Non-algebraicity of non-abundant foliations and abundance for adjoint foliated structures
papers.abstract: Assuming the abundance conjecture in dimension $d$, we establish a non-algebraicity criterion of foliations: any log canonical foliation of rank $\le d$ with $ν\neqκ$ is not algebraically integrable, answering question of Ambro--Cascini--Shokurov--Spicer. Under the same hypothesis, we prove abundance for klt algebraically integrable adjoint foliated structures of dimension $\le d$ and show the existence of good minimal models or Mori fiber spaces. In particular, when $d=3$, all these results hold unconditionally. Using similar arguments, we solve a problem proposed by Lu and Wu on abundance of surface adjoint foliated structures that are not necessarily algebraically integrable.

papers.title: Two stage GNSS outlier detection for factor graph optimization based GNSS-RTK/INS/odometer fusion
papers.abstract: GNSS pseudorange outliers severely disturb carrier-phase ambiguity resolution and positioning, particularly during signal blockages and recovery. Temporal Doppler consistency provides a reliable short-term range-change reference, but requires valid measurements at both endpoints and becomes unavailable upon signal re-acquisition. This paper presents a two-stage pseudorange screening framework that complements Doppler consistency with joint IMU-odometer motion prediction. The second stage compares predicted and measured temporal changes of double-differenced pseudoranges against an accepted anchor epoch without using current GNSS observations in the motion reference. A first-order error model separates anchor, relative-motion, and measurement uncertainties to propagate factor-graph covariance into the chi-square detection gate, and both stages adjust code weights through a closed-form minimum-inflation rule. Under continuous tracking, Doppler screening reduces RTK 3D RMSE by 96.18% and outperforms the a-contrario baseline by 58.56%. When Doppler checks are unavailable, joint IMU-odometer prediction detects a 10-m outlier change in 99.58% of trials after 30 s and 73.72% after 60 s, reducing RIO 3D RMSE by up to 78.51% after outages while RI screening outperforms an inertial-aided baseline by 70.42% in simulation and 39.11% in deep urban canyons.

papers.title: UniSage: A Unified and Diagnosis-Driven Sampling Framework for Microservice Systems
papers.abstract: Traces and logs are essential observability signals for diagnosing microservice failures, but their massive volume makes full retention prohibitively expensive. Sampling is therefore widely used to reduce storage and analysis overhead. However, existing sampling frameworks suffer from two key limitations. First, they typically follow a sample-before-analysis paradigm, where data is discarded before its diagnostic value is known, risking the loss of critical evidence for downstream analysis. Second, they mainly focus on trace sampling, while logs are either compressed or filtered independently, which can break the contextual linkage between anomalous traces and their explanatory log messages. To address these limitations, we propose UniSage, a unified and diagnosis-driven sampling framework for microservice systems. UniSage is unified in two senses: it integrates lightweight analysis into the sampling pipeline to guide retention decisions, and it jointly samples traces and logs by exploiting their cross-modal correlations. Evaluations on three multi-modal microservice datasets show that UniSage consistently preserves more diagnostic evidence under tight budgets. At the 5% budget, UniSage improves average diagnostic trace recall by 6.8%-22.0% over existing trace sampling baselines and achieves the highest diagnostic log recall on the evaluated log-labeled datasets. UniSage also remains practical, with runtime measurements showing modest overhead across the evaluated workloads.

papers.title: Membership Inference Attacks on Recommender System: A Survey
papers.abstract: Recommender systems (RecSys) have been widely applied across e-commerce, finance, healthcare, and social media and have become increasingly influential in shaping user behavior and decision-making, underscoring their growing impact across domains. Since RecSys heavily relies on user data, its privacy concerns are significant and need to be addressed urgently. Recent studies on membership inference attacks (MIAs) in RecSys highlight this need. MIAs aim to infer whether a user or an interaction record was used to train a target RecSys model. Successful MIAs can lead to severe privacy breaches, such as revealing sensitive aspects of users' lifestyles. MIAs in RecSys have features distinct from those targeting classification models or large language models. However, no systematic survey on this topic has yet been conducted. We present the first comprehensive survey on RecSys MIAs, exploring their taxonomy, design principles, evaluation methods, and defense mechanisms. Based on the summary of existing studies in this area, we also outline several promising future research directions. This survey aims to raise awareness of privacy risks among RecSys researchers, practitioners, and users, and promote privacy protection practices in RecSys design.

papers.title: ReST-RL: Reinforcing LLM Reasoning through Unified Self-Training and Value-Guided Search
papers.abstract: With respect to improving the reasoning accuracy of LLMs, the representative reinforcement learning (RL) method - Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) - has achieved critical success, yet it still suffers from the issue of insignificant reward signals. This paper introduces ReST-RL, a unified Reinforced Self-Training (ReST) policy-value framework that reconnects policy optimization and value-guided search to improve LLM reasoning ability. Firstly, ReST-GRPO adopts an optimized ReST-style algorithm to reshape the policy-induced trajectory distribution by increasing the reward variance of GRPO sampling and exposing the policy to more informative partial states, thereby improving training efficiency and effectiveness. Then, we further introduce a decoding optimization method, VM-MCTS, which trains a Value Model (VM) from self-collected Monte-Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) targets and deploys it through an adapted MCTS algorithm to provide precise process signals and verification scores, further enhancing reasoning accuracy. These two stages are internally dependent - ReST-GRPO yields higher quality trajectories for value learning with VM-MCTS, which in turn enables more effective inference-time search. We validate our framework on multiple coding benchmarks (e.g., APPS, BigCodeBench, and HumanEval), where it significantly outperforms other reinforcement training baselines (naive GRPO, DAPO, and ReST-DPO), as well as decoding and verification baselines (e.g., PRM-BoN and ORM-MCTS), indicating its power to strengthen LLM reasoning capability. Moreover, we further evaluate ReST-RL on out-of-domain math and science reasoning tasks, where it achieves improved performance without target-domain tuning and favorable end-to-end efficiency trade-offs, providing preliminary transfer evidence beyond our primary coding domain.

papers.title: Symbolic Branch Networks: Tree-Inherited Neural Models for Interpretable Multiclass Classification
papers.abstract: Symbolic Branch Networks (SBNs) are neural models whose architecture is derived directly from an ensemble of decision trees. Each root-to-parent-of-leaf decision path is mapped to a hidden neuron, while the matrices W1 (feature-to-branch) and W2 (branch-to-class) encode the structural relationships induced by the teacher ensemble. This provides an explicit correspondence between teacher branches and neural components, enabling feature-level and branch-level interpretation while retaining the flexibility of gradient-based optimization. The primary configuration studied in this work trains the teacher-derived feature-to-branch matrix W1 through gradient-based learning while keeping the branch-to-class matrix W2 fixed; this configuration is denoted SBN1,0. Across 29 multiclass tabular datasets, this configuration improves upon the teacher ensemble on 28 of 29 datasets, increasing mean accuracy from 84.0% to 87.9%. For reference, XGBoost and TabPFN achieve mean accuracies of 87.3% and 91.3%, respectively, on the same datasets. A one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test on dataset-level mean accuracies indicates a statistically significant improvement of SBN1,0 over the teacher ensemble (p=4.71x10-7). Beyond predictive performance, SBN provides an explicit structural basis for interpretation. Global feature importance can be derived from the teacher-induced feature-to-branch connectivity, while individual predictions can be traced to selected branch-neurons, their associated features, and their class contributions. An analysis across ten independently constructed teacher ensembles shows consistent predictions for a selected instance but only partial stability in its local feature rankings.

papers.title: EDGChain-E: A Decentralized Git-Based Framework for Versioning Encrypted Energy Data
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a new decentralized framework, named EDGChain-E (Encrypted-Data-Git Chain for Energy), designed to manage version-controlled, encrypted energy data using blockchain and the InterPlanetary File System. The framework incorporates a Decentralized Autonomous Organization (DAO) to orchestrate collaborative data governance across the lifecycle of energy research and operations, such as smart grid monitoring, demand forecasting, and peer-to-peer energy trading. In EDGChain-E, initial commits capture the full encrypted datasets-such as smart meter readings or grid telemetry-while subsequent updates are tracked as encrypted Git patches, ensuring integrity, traceability, and privacy. This versioning mechanism supports secure collaboration across multiple stakeholders (e.g., utilities, researchers, regulators) without compromising sensitive or regulated information. We highlight the framework's capability to maintain FAIR-compliant (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) provenance of encrypted data. By embedding hash-based content identifiers in Merkle trees, the system enables transparent, auditable, and immutable tracking of data changes, thereby supporting reproducibility and trust in decentralized energy applications.

papers.title: BitBypass: A New Direction in Jailbreaking Aligned Large Language Models with Bitstream Camouflage
papers.abstract: The inherent risk of generating harmful and unsafe content by Large Language Models (LLMs), has highlighted the need for their safety alignment. Various techniques like supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning from human feedback, and red-teaming were developed for ensuring the safety alignment of LLMs. However, the robustness of these aligned LLMs is always challenged by adversarial attacks that exploit unexplored and underlying vulnerabilities of the safety alignment. In this paper, we develop a novel black-box jailbreak attack, called BitBypass, that leverages hyphen-separated bitstream camouflage for jailbreaking aligned LLMs. This represents a new direction in jailbreaking by exploiting fundamental information representation of data as continuous bits, rather than leveraging prompt engineering or adversarial manipulations. Our evaluation of five state-of-the-art LLMs, namely GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5, Claude 3.5, Llama 3.1, and Mixtral, in adversarial perspective, revealed the capabilities of BitBypass in bypassing their safety alignment and tricking them into generating harmful and unsafe content. Further, we observed that BitBypass outperforms several state-of-the-art jailbreak attacks in terms of stealthiness and attack success. Overall, these results highlights the effectiveness and efficiency of BitBypass in jailbreaking these state-of-the-art LLMs.

papers.title: LiteLMGuard: Seamless and Lightweight On-Device Guardrails for Small Language Models against Quantization Vulnerabilities
papers.abstract: The growing adoption of Large Language Models (LLMs) has influenced the development of Small Language Models (SLMs) for on-device deployment across smartphones and edge devices, offering enhanced privacy, reduced latency, server-free functionality, and improved user experience. However, due to on-device resource constraints, SLMs undergo size optimization through compression techniques like quantization, which inadvertently introduce fairness, ethical and privacy risks. Critically, quantized SLMs may respond to harmful queries directly, without requiring adversarial manipulation, raising significant safety and trust concerns. To address this, we propose LiteLMGuard, an on-device guardrail that provides real-time, prompt-level defense for quantized SLMs. Additionally, our guardrail is designed to be model-agnostic such that it can be seamlessly integrated with any SLM, operating independently of underlying architectures. Our LiteLMGuard formalizes deep learning (DL)-based prompt filtering by leveraging semantic understanding to classify prompt answerability for SLMs. Built on our curated Answerable-or-Not dataset, LiteLMGuard employs ELECTRA as the candidate model with 97.75% answerability classification accuracy. The on-device deployment of LiteLMGuard enabled real-time offline filtering with over 85% defense-rate against harmful prompts (including jailbreak attacks), 94% filtering accuracy and ~135 ms average latency. These results demonstrate LiteLMGuard as a lightweight robust defense mechanism for effectively and efficiently securing on-device SLMs against Open Knowledge Attacks.

papers.title: Near-Optimal Techniques for Distributed Entanglement Generation and Purification
papers.abstract: We develop a purification-aware optimization framework for distributing high-fidelity entangled states over quantum networks. In repeater-based architectures, the framework jointly selects entanglement swapping, fusion or graph-state growth, and purification operations to maximize generation rate under a fidelity threshold. Different purification models can be incorporated through their fidelity-update, success-probability, and latency rules. We introduce purification-augmented generation trees and dynamic programming (DP) algorithms for entangled-pair (EP) distribution. Hypergraph-flow linear programming (LP) formulations support level-based structures and concurrent generation across multiple trees and demands. We extend the framework to GHZ states and arbitrary graph states constructed from remote EP resources, introduce graph-state construction primitives, and derive closed-form fidelity-vector updates for GHZ fusion and purification and graph-state growth and purification. We provide optimal formulations under the adopted models, discretization, and purification bounds, together with efficient DP and LP heuristics. We bound fidelity- and rate-discretization errors and establish convergence for fixed constructions under stated regularity conditions. NetSquid simulations of EP generation using our LP approach show an average 160% increase in generation rate over the compared prior approaches, with gains up to 330% in some scenarios. GHZ and graph-state simulations demonstrate the heuristics' effectiveness in balancing generation rate, output fidelity, and computational overhead.

papers.title: On quaternionic analysis and a certain generalized fractal-fractional $ψ$-Fueter operator
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a fractal $ψ$-Fueter operator in the quaternionic context inspired by the concepts of proportional derivative and Hausdorff derivative ({fractal derivative}) of a function with respect to a fractal measure. Moreover, we establish the corresponding Stokes and Borel-Pompeiu formulas associated to this generalized fractal $ψ$-Fueter operator with respect to a vector valued function induced by truncated exponential functions.

papers.title: The infinitesimal subgroup of interpretable groups in some dp-minimal valued fields
papers.abstract: We continue our local analysis of groups interpretable in various dp-minimal valued fields, as introduced in [8]. We associate with every infinite group $G$ interpretable in those fields an infinite type-definable infinitesimal subgroup $ν(G)$, generated by the four infinitesimal subgroups $ν_D(G)$ associated with the distinguished sorts $K$, $\textbf{k}$, $Γ$ and $K/\mathcal{O}$. To show that $ν(G)$ is type-definable, we show that the resulting subgroups $ν_D(G)$ commute with each other as $D$ ranges over the four distinguished sorts. We then study the basic properties of $ν(G)$. Among others, we show that $ν(G_1\times G_2)=ν(G_1)\times ν(G_2)$ and that if $G_1\le G$ is a definable subgroup then $ν(G_1)$ is relatively definable in $ν(G)$. We also discuss possible connections between $\mathrm{dp\text{-}rk}(ν(G))$ and elimination of imaginaries.

papers.title: Explicit expressions for iterates of power series
papers.abstract: We present several formulas for both the discrete and fractional iterates of an invertible power series $f,$ using a new unifying approach based on umbral calculus. Known formulas are extended, and their proofs simplified, while new expressions are introduced. In particular, by employing $q$-calculus identities, we eliminate the requirement for $f'(0)$ to equal $1$ and the resulting general expressions for the iterative logarithm are also obtained.

papers.title: Finding pure Nash equilibria in large random games
papers.abstract: Best Response Dynamics (BRD) constitute a family of strategy update rules designed to identify Pure Nash Equilibria (PNEs) in strategic games. In each iteration, a player is selected uniformly at random and adopts a best response strategy, maximising their payoff given the current strategies of the other players. If no improvement is possible for the selected player, another is chosen. The process terminates upon reaching a state where no player wishes to deviate, corresponding to a PNE. However, convergence is not guaranteed as either PNEs may not exist, or the dynamics may become confined within substructures of the game, which we call traps, that admit no PNEs. We investigate this behaviour in the context of random games with $N$ players, each choosing between two actions and receiving independently and identically distributed payoffs. The payoff distribution is permitted to have atoms, allowing for the possibility of ties. The induced dynamics define a class of random walks on the $N$-dimensional hypercube, where the landscape includes two types of absorbing sets: PNEs and traps. Our analysis encompasses BRD, simple random walks, and a broad class of nearest-neighbour processes. We prove that, with high probability, these dynamics reach a PNE before encountering any trap. Our results complete and generalise the ones by Amiet, Collevecchio, Scarsini and Zhong (2021), using a different approach.

papers.title: Minimal submanifolds and stability in Einstein manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper, we compute the index and nullity for minimal submanifolds of some complex Einstein spaces. We investigate the stability of these minimal submanifolds and suggest a criterion for instability for some cases. We also compute some higher eigenvalues for the Laplacian of the Berger spheres and provide with an algorithm.

papers.title: Credible Sets of Overall Ranking of Entities
papers.abstract: Ranking, and inferences based on ranking of a set of entities, are important problems in numerous contexts. This is especially true in small area statistics where there may be only a limited amount of directly observed data from each entity or small area, while precise and accurate estimates of best or worst performing entities are needed for fund allocation, planning and policymaking, stakeholder advocacy, evaluation of welfare programs, and so on. However, ranks estimates constructed exclusively on point estimates of parameters lack uncertainty quantification, and may lead to imbalances and inequities when these are based on small sample sizes. We propose novel Bayesian approaches to address this problem. Our proposals result in partitions of the parameter space with posterior distribution driven partial ordering of the sets in a partition. This in turn translates to a coherent probability mass function over ranks for every entity, and a coherent probability mass function over entities for every rank. Our Bayesian algorithms significantly outperform the state-of-the-art non-Bayesian alternatives, and are amenable to inclusion of covariates in the model as well as borrowing strengths across small areas. We evaluate our proposed Bayesian algorithms in terms of accuracy and stability using a number of applications and a simulation study. Additionally, we develop a novel theoretical framework for inference and ranking problems involving a triangular array of Fay-Herriot models and data, and provide probabilistic guarantees of performances of the proposed Bayesian ranking algorithms.

papers.title: Ordinals and recursively defined functions on the reals
papers.abstract: We determine sufficient conditions under which certain recursively defined functions are well defined for all real inputs. Given a function $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, call a decreasing sequence $x_1>x_2>x_3>\cdots$ "$f$-bad" if $f(x_1)>f(x_2)>f(x_3)>\cdots$, and call the function $f$ "ordinal decreasing" if there exist no infinite $f$-bad sequences. We prove the following result: Given ordinal decreasing functions $f,g_1,\ldots,g_k,s$ that are everywhere larger than $0$, define the recursive algorithm "$M(x)$: if $x<0$ return $f(x)$, else return $g_1(-M(x-g_2(-M(x-\cdots-g_k(-M(x-s(x)))\cdots))))$". Then $M(x)$ halts and is ordinal decreasing for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$. The recursive algorithms $M$ and $M_n$ previously studied in the context of fusible numbers by Ericskon et al. (2022) and Bufetov et al. (2024), respectively, are special cases of this scheme. Moreover, given an ordinal decreasing function $f$, denote by $o(f)$ the ordinal height of the root of the tree of $f$-bad sequences. Then we prove that, for $k\ge 2$, the function $M(x)$ defined by the above algorithm satisfies $o(M)\leφ_{k-1}(γ+o(s)+1)$, where $γ$ is the smallest ordinal such that $\max\{o(s),o(f),o(g_1), \ldots, o(g_k)\} <φ_{k-1}(γ)$.

papers.title: On minimal subshifts of linear word complexity with slope less than 3/2
papers.abstract: We prove that every infinite minimal subshift with word complexity $p(q)$ satisfying $\limsup p(q)/q < 3/2$ is measure-theoretically isomorphic to its maximal equicontinuous factor; in particular, it has measurably discrete spectrum. Among other applications, this provides a proof of Sarnak's conjecture for all subshifts with $\limsup p(q)/q < 3/2$ (which can be thought of as a much stronger version of zero entropy). We also show that all such subshifts are balanced, and that orbit equivalence between them is characterized by the additive eigenvalue group. As in [CP23], our main technique is proving that all low-complexity minimal subshifts have a specific type of representation via a sequence $\{τ_k\}$ of substitutions, usually called an S-adic decomposition. The maximal equicontinuous factor is the (possibly twisted) product of an odometer with a rotation on a compact abelian connected one-dimensional group (either a circle or solenoid), for which we can give an explicit description in terms of the substitutions $τ_k$. We also prove that all such odometers and groups may appear for minimal subshifts with $\limsup p(q)/q = 1$, demonstrating that lower complexity thresholds do not further restrict the possible structure.

papers.title: Almost Sure Averaging for Fast-slow Stochastic Differential Equations via Controlled Rough Path
papers.abstract: This paper establishes the averaging method to a coupled system consisting of two stochastic differential equations which has a slow component driven by fractional Brownian motion (FBM) with less regularity $1/3< H \leq 1/2$ and a fast dynamics under additive FBM with Hurst-index $1/3< \hat H \leq 1/2$. We prove that the solution of the slow component converges almost surely to the solution of the corresponding averaged equation using the approach of time discretization and controlled rough path. To do this, we employ the random dynamical system (RDS) to obtain a stationary solution by an exponentially attracting random fixed point of the RDS generated by the non-Markovian fast component.

papers.title: EnKF-C user guide
papers.abstract: EnKF-C provides a compact generic framework for off-line data assimilation into large-scale layered geophysical models with the ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF). It is coded in C for GNU/Linux platform and can work either in EnKF, ensemble optimal interpolation (EnOI), or hybrid (EnKF/EnOI) modes.

papers.title: Spontaneous mechanical patterning in active elastic tissues with stress feedback
papers.abstract: The active mechanics of biological tissues is often governed by embedded active contractile fibers responding to mechanical feedback. We introduce a minimal model of a solid-like tissue where the mechanics is controlled by feedback of local active and elastic stresses on fiber organization. The resulting tissue generically exhibits a bistable response to external strain and spontaneously segregates into domains of orthogonally aligned fibers. Our theory thus provides a minimal mechanical feedback mechanism generating orthogonal structural alignment ubiquitous in biological tissues.

papers.title: Feedback-induced mechanical bistability and perpendicular-domain formation in active elastic tissues
papers.abstract: Contractile fibers in muscle tissues are highly aligned over the scale of many cells. Muscle layers surrounding organs with an inner lumen are often arranged in orthogonal directions. Here, we study a minimal mechanism of how structural order and its patterning into orthogonally aligned domains can emerge from mechanical feedback alone. The central idea is that contractile fibers align in the direction of the local active and elastic stresses, a feedback motivated by the maturation of muscle fibers under tension. We thus model muscle tissue as an active nematic solid with stress feedback: an elastic medium with embedded contractile fibers that are reinforced along the directions of the local tissue stresses. We find that the feedback from the contractile fiber stress is self-amplifying and drives spontaneous fiber alignment. Feedback from the elastic stress couples the alignment to the mechanical boundary conditions and tissue geometry. Depending on the mechanical boundary conditions, the elastic-stress feedback stabilizes two orthogonally aligned tissue states, resulting in a structurally and mechanically bistable tissue that shows a hysteretic stress-strain response. In spatially extended tissues, this bistability gives rise to orthogonally aligned domains separated by domain walls. Our results show that stress feedback can pattern structural order by coupling spontaneous alignment to the tissue geometry. Our mechanism thus provides a purely mechanical route to orthogonal fiber patterning in muscle tissues.

papers.title: Driving World Models Move the Camera, Not the Scene
papers.abstract: Plan-conditioned driving world models are used to compare candidate plans, so their forecast should change with the plan as the real scene would, yet widely used control metrics check only whether the camera follows the command. Recorded drives already contain real outcomes of plans that were never driven: retiming a log gives pose-matched images and LiDAR for other speeds, and a stereo rig records a laterally shifted view. Against these references, released world models move their camera but barely move the scene: their scene response, the share of the real change in distance that the forecast reproduces, reaches at most about a third of real video's, and the trajectory score cannot tell an executed speed command from an ignored one. Interventions inside the generator trace the failure to the plan's channel. The forecast geometry follows the context frames; once they carry the planned geometry, plan tokens add little. ReTime-Compose therefore delivers the plan as geometry, without training. It transports the frames of one logged-speed rollout to the planned cameras, and the frozen model completes only what no frame covers. Frozen generators then follow a 0.54 m lateral shift nearly as the real scene does on KITTI, nuScenes and Argoverse 2, and respond more than re-sampling to slow-down plans in three generators and to speed-up plans in two.

papers.title: An Analytical Model for Fast Design Optimization and Performance Studies of nuSTORM
papers.abstract: The concept of generating neutrino beams from stored muons (nuSTORM) has been explored for several decades. A few nuSTORM facilities have been designed for GeV muons, and a design of a sub-GeV nuSTORM, proposed for the European Spallation Source, is now underway. At low energy, the much larger beam divergence can significantly reduce the neutrino flux reaching the detector. Therefore, optimization of facility parameters is essential to avoid additional flux losses. This optimization, however, is not trivial due to the interdependency of the parameters. In this paper, we derive an analytical expression for the absolute neutrino flux incident on the detector front face and show how it can guide the optimization of a nuSTORM facility. The analytical expression is furthermore validated with published data and Monte Carlo simulations from five separate cases. In addition, we show how it can be extended to also predict the neutrino energy distribution at the detector, thus offering a convenient method to estimate the facility performance without time-consuming Monte Carlo simulations of particle transport and decay.
authors: J. P. A. M. de André

papers.title: Exact transformation-optics representation of the Ellis wormhole and limits of finite-device scattering emulation
papers.abstract: We derive a global isotropic representation of the ultrastatic Ellis wormhole and establish which features of its electromagnetic response can, and cannot, be reproduced by a finite device. An orientation-preserving coordinate map sends the signed proper-radial line to a punctured Euclidean chart with refractive index $n(ρ)=1+a^2/(4ρ^2)$. Through the Plebański correspondence, this gives the exact impedance-matched continuum medium $\varepsilon_r=μ_r=n(ρ)\mathbf{I}$ and its full vector-Maxwell operator. For the ideal two-ended geometry, we derive the electromagnetic radial operator, establish its spectral properties, and express its scattering amplitudes through Jost solutions and Wronskians. Nonzero transmission into the second asymptotic end implies $|R_{\rm id}|<1$ at every real frequency, whereas a regular, lossless finite one-port has unit-modulus reflection. The reverse triangle inequality therefore yields a strictly positive lower bound on the complex reflection-amplitude mismatch. This theorem applies to the stated lossless single-port class and is not extended to lossy or multiport realizations. We compute converged multipole scattering data and establish the low-frequency threshold scaling $|T_L|^2\propto(ωa/c)^{4L+2}$, with coefficients independently validated for $L=1,2,3,4$. The transmission cross section tends to $πa^2$, while the ideal profile's total scattering cross section has a logarithmic forward divergence. We also construct a smooth finite-shell target and derive an exact finite-band constitutive-error formula for a calibrated passive Lorentz model. The constitutive benchmark is kept distinct from scattering equivalence throughout.

papers.title: Owned Edits to a Shared Decision Rule: Learning Private Exceptions as Typed, Gated, Withdrawable Weight Edits
papers.abstract: Organisations that apply the same published decision rule often hold private evidence that the rule is wrong for their own cases, and will not pool it. We describe a learning mechanism for that setting whose unit of change is an owned edit. The published rule is compiled exactly into a small ReLU network, a structured prior. Each party's learner searches a small typed space of declarations, a few named values such as subject, scope, form and size, and proposes one only when its own records pass a selection-aware evidence gate. The learning is that gated search around the prior.
