In two pre-registered analyses, on synthetic data whose 20 hidden truths were sampled from that typed space, the learner at 30 records per party was non-inferior, within 2 points, to all seven tuned baselines (a confined gradient learner, Ditto, FedRep, federated averaging, two pooled networks and pooled boosted trees), scoring 96.6% against 91.7% for the unchanged rule; a descriptive greedy ablation with no prior, over a separate space, scored 84.0%. In a third registered test, typed edits over a network trained on shared records beat that network alone by +5.4 points and the same edits over the published rule by +3.1; oracle-tuned fine-tuning and Ditto matched it at 30 records. An acceptance body recomputes each edit from its declaration and writes it into units reserved for that party, so by construction an edit changes no decision about any other subject, withdraws exactly, discloses at most log2 of the typed space's size in bits, and the artefact can hide nothing beyond its declared values; timing is not covered. We report where it loses: truths shared by all parties, relaxations, ten records, a pre-stated gate criterion that failed in both runs, and a language model given the records that decided about as accurately on one draw. On a rule-only base, a table of owned exceptions makes the same decisions.

papers.title: Runtime Analysis of Cartesian Genetic Programming on Max: A Proven Exponential Speedup
papers.abstract: Genetic Programming (GP) is a search paradigm inspired from natural evolution for the automated discovery of expressions, functions, and computer programs. Cartesian GP (CGP) is a flavor of GP that uses a graph-based model to encode candidate programs, as contrasted to the conventional Tree-based GP (TGP). Since its inception two decades ago, CGP has predominantly been analyzed empirically, thus little is known regarding its theoretical performance guarantees. This paper analyzes CGP for the Max problem, which has been only rigorously studied for TGP with a proven expected runtime superlinear in the optimal program length $n$. We prove that the expected time for the ($1$+$1$) CGP employing common mutation operators to evolve an equivalent optimal of the same output is polylogarithmic in $n$, specifically at most $O(\log^9{n})$. This is remarkable, as it shows an exponential speedup by switching to CGP. Our results shed light on the benefit and the compactness of the graph-based representation for programs, and on how CGP can navigate its search and fitness spaces efficiently. This is a first proven performance guarantee for CGP on an established benchmark problem. Experiments complement our theoretical findings.

papers.title: Residual-Tail-Informed Flow Matching for Time Series Anomaly Detection
papers.abstract: Time series anomaly detection (TSAD) models are often trained on nominal data using average-risk objectives, which emphasize dominant normal patterns. However, real time series can contain rare but valid nominal regimes that are underrepresented in the training distribution. We show that data-space flow matching can over-penalize such rare-normal windows and assign them anomaly scores comparable to those of true anomalies. To address this, we propose Residual-Tail-Informed Flow Matching (RT-FM), an unsupervised framework that uses a temporal variational autoencoder to estimate residual latent tailness and converts it into bounded, warmup-annealed weights for training a data-space flow matching model. Experiments on seven TSAD benchmarks show that RT-FM improves rare-normal coverage while preserving strong anomaly discrimination, substantially reducing false alarms on such windows and resulting in improved aggregate detection performance. The code is available at: https://github.com/trustAIoT/RT-FM_time-series-anomaly

papers.title: Beyond Service Discovery: Coverage Awareness in LLM-Driven Service Composition
papers.abstract: Large language models increasingly support the automated discovery and composition of services. In federated data ecosystems, this creates new opportunities for reusing existing data products and transformation services when constructing service-based data exchange modeled as data-sharing pipelines. However, finding relevant reusable assets does not imply that the available assets are sufficient to satisfy a consumer request. In this paper, we distinguish reuse discovery, the ability to identify relevant published assets, from reuse coverage, the extent to which the available assets support the transformations required by a request. We further consider coverage awareness, the ability of a composition system to recognize insufficient coverage. We investigate this distinction using PipeFinder, an LLM-driven framework for composing data-sharing pipelines, and evaluate 99 consumer requests against a fixed catalogue of data products and transformation services. Our experiments show that relevant data products can be discovered reliably, while successful composition remains considerably more difficult. More importantly, when required transformation services are missing, the framework typically constructs a pipeline from the available services rather than recognizing that the request cannot be satisfied. Explicitly incorporating coverage checking into the planning procedure substantially improves recognition of such cases. These results suggest that coverage awareness should be treated as an explicit concern in LLM-driven service composition and cannot be assumed to follow from improved discovery or model capability.

papers.title: The monogenicity of $\boldsymbol{x^n+c\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}a^{n-j-1}x^j}$
papers.abstract: We say that a monic polynomial $f(x)\in {\mathbb Z}[x]$ is {\em monogenic} if $f(x)$ is irreducible over ${\mathbb Q}$ and $\{1,θ,θ^2,\ldots,θ^{{\rm deg}(f)-1}\}$ is a basis for the ring of integers of ${\mathbb Q}(θ)$, where $f(θ)=0$. Let $n,a,c\in {\mathbb Z}$ with $n\ge 3$, and suppose that \[{\mathcal F}_{n,a,c}(x):=x^n+cx^{n-1}+acx^{n-2}+a^2cx^{n-3}+\cdots +a^{n-2}cx+a^{n-1}c\] is irreducible over ${\mathbb Q}$. Recently, Jakhar, Kalwaniya and Yadav have given necessary and sufficient conditions for the monogenicity of ${\mathcal F}_{n,a,c}(x)$, under the assumption that all prime divisors of the discriminant of ${\mathcal F}_{n,a,c}(x)$ not dividing $ac$ also do not divide $n+1$. In this note, we provide necessary and sufficient conditions for the monogenicity of ${\mathcal F}_{n,a,c}(x)$ without this restriction.

papers.title: LENS: Replacing LayerNorm and Softmax in Transformers with Learnable Normalization States
papers.abstract: LayerNorm and attention Softmax are critical operations in Transformers. However, they cannot be efficiently mapped to General Matrix Multiplication (GEMM) computations on hardware. Therefore, modern hardware accelerator designs, such as NPUs on ASIC/FPGA, consume a large amount of hardware resources or chip area to implement their specific arithmetic units. Building on previous work about LayerNorm, Softmax, and their alternatives, we introduce Learnable Normalization States (LENS), a framework that reformulates LayerNorm as tiny MLPs by abstracting a common structure from related methods and extends this method to Softmax, which moves more of the computation in Transformers to GEMM as a hardware-friendly architecture. We evaluate LENS on image classification with Vision Transformers (ViT) and autoregressive language modeling with Pythia models, including generalization tests on WikiText and LAMBADA. Across these tasks, LENS matches or exceeds baseline performance in several vision settings and retains most of the baseline performance in the remaining vision and language experiments. These findings may suggest that hand-designed normalization and attention functions are not the only choice as alternatives to LayerNorm and Softmax. LENS also provides a basis for exploring Transformer architectures for resource-limited accelerators.

papers.title: Sidewalk Stewards: A Visual Analytics Approach for Interactive Topology Repair of Sidewalk Networks
papers.abstract: Accurate pedestrian network data is foundational to urban accessibility, routing, and infrastructure planning, yet such data remains scarce and difficult to produce at scale. Automated extraction pipelines have made significant strides by leveraging computer vision to derive sidewalk networks from aerial imagery, and have seen real-world adoption by municipalities seeking cost-effective inventory solutions. Yet, these pipelines consistently produce topological errors (e.g., disconnected components, dangling edges, missed connections, malformed intersections) that undermine the utility of the extracted networks for routing and accessibility analysis. Correcting these errors requires situated human judgment that global automated repair strategies cannot replicate, yet practitioners currently lack dedicated tools to support this work efficiently. We present Sidewalk Stewards, a visual analytics system that bridges the gap between automated extraction and a deployment-ready pedestrian network. Sidewalk Stewards detects candidate topology errors, supports interactive user-guided correction through coordinated spatial views, and provides real-time quality feedback as edits are applied. We evaluate Sidewalk Stewards through a comparative user study, case studies across cities, and a quantitative evaluation. Compared with conventional workflows, the system facilitates error identification and enables faster and more complete correction. The case studies illustrate the workflow across different urban contexts, and the quantitative evaluation shows that a small number of user corrections can enhance multiple sidewalk quality metrics. Sidewalk Stewards is available at urbantk.org/sidewalk.

papers.title: Ternary-Valued FDTD Method for Nonlinear Optics: Third-Harmonic Generation on a Multiplier-Free Solver
papers.abstract: I show that a finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) solver with field variables restricted to the ternary alphabet $\{-1,0,+1\}$ can reproduce nonlinear optical physics quantitatively on both CPUs and field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs). Building on the general ternary-valued FDTD algorithm, in which each Yee cell stores an integer state that accumulates the discrete curl of neighbouring symbols without being drained, I extend the scheme to inhomogeneous and Kerr media and to Mur absorbing boundaries, without performing any multiplication operations. Dielectric contrast is implemented as a multiplexer, since the difference between ternary symbols takes only a few values, the instantaneous Kerr nonlinearity as a coefficient look-up table and the Mur boundary coefficients as canonical signed-digit shift--add chains. The scheme reproduces the third-harmonic conversion efficiency of a floating-point reference to within $1.4\%$. A symmetry of the governing physics, expressed through the even harmonics forbidden by centrosymmetric $χ^{(3)}$, provides a reference-free self-check for both ternary and floating-point models. The complete solver fits on a small, low-cost FPGA and contains no multiplier anywhere in its datapath, placing nonlinear optical modelling within reach of embedded and autonomous platforms rather than of high-performance computers.

papers.title: Phase Structure and Thermodynamic Geometry of STU Black Holes
papers.abstract: We study the thermodynamics of four-dimensional STU black holes, a family of charged solutions of gauged N = 8, SO(8) supergravity, from the perspective of geometric thermodynamics. We focus on non-rotating solutions carrying pairwise-equal charges, obtaining closed-form expressions for the thermodynamic quantities directly in terms of the physical charges, and use them to determine the equation of state and associated phase structure. We also construct the Ruppeiner geometry for the STU black hole, taking the temperature and thermodynamic volume as fluctuation variables, and study its renormalized curvature as a probe of the black hole microstructure. We find a rich phase structure with two critical points present whenever the charge ratio is sufficiently large, and identify regions in parameter space associated with attractive and repulsive microscopic interactions.

papers.title: Exceptional structure and Lifshitz criticality in a non-Hermitian Kitaev chain
papers.abstract: We study an exactly solvable non-Hermitian $N$-site Kitaev chain with unequal pair-creation and pair-annihilation amplitudes and vanishing intersite hopping. We show that the chain supports an exceptional point (EP) at which all the many-body energies collapse to zero and the largest Jordan block grows quadratically with $N$. By constructing an explicit positive metric for the associated $N$-dimensional one-body problem which admits an extension to the full many-body Hamiltonian, we demonstrate that this EP collapse can be approached through a continuous quasi-Hermitian path in the parameter space. Further, in a different regime with onsite energies alternating between two unequal positive values, we show that pairing amplitudes of opposite signs can lead to crossings between ground states of opposite fermion parity within a quasi-Hermitian regime. Their accumulation in the thermodynamic limit produces a Lifshitz transition, characterized by particle-/hole-pocket formation, quadratic critical dispersion, and a nonanalytic ground-state energy density. We show that this transition remains separated from the EP boundary and ceases to exist for balanced real pairing.

papers.title: Simulating access to alcohol screening, brief intervention, referral to and receipt of specialty treatment for alcohol use disorder in California and Texas: A study protocol for an agent-based modeling study (AUDTxSim)
papers.abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) affects millions of US adults. Primary care-based screening, brief intervention, and referral to treatment (SBIRT) is a leading strategy for identifying heavy drinking early, but access to primary care, screening, and specialty treatment differs markedly across subgroups. Whether scaling SBIRT and expanding treatment capacity narrows or widens these differences is unknown and cannot feasibly be tested in a randomized trial. We present AUDTxSim (AUD Treatment Simulation), a stochastic, spatially explicit, individual-based model of alcohol use, AUD, SBIRT, and specialty treatment for the adult populations of California and Texas. Agents represent every adult in synthetic populations of the two states (28.0 and 19.3 million adults), each geo-located to a Census tract and linked to nearby treatment facilities. In daily time steps, the model simulates: (1) annual transitions among eight alcohol use and AUD states; (2) healthcare visits, screening, brief intervention, and referral; (3) treatment seeking, standalone medication for AUD, mutual help, and requests for hospitalization, residential, or outpatient care; (4) a treatment manager that allocates individuals to facilities by preference, geography, and capacity, with telehealth substitution and waitlists; and (5) treatment progression, stepdown between levels of care, and post-treatment mutual help. It is implemented in Python with Repast4Py to run in parallel on a computing cluster. Once calibrated to state, rural-urban, and demographic targets for healthcare visits, heavy drinking and AUD prevalence, and mortality, AUDTxSim will project population-level and subgroup-specific effects of alternative SBIRT reach and treatment capacity scenarios on AUD prevalence, treatment receipt, and mortality. We report the model structure, decision logic, data sources, and calibration plan.

papers.title: Measuring Coherence in Predictive Models
papers.abstract: Many sequential decision-making procedures, such as active learning, implicitly assume that a model's current predictions agree with those it expects to make after updating on new data, a property we call coherence. Most models in use do not update by exact conditioning and are not guaranteed to be coherent, which can lead to worse decisions. Yet there is currently no general way to measure incoherence or to tell when it matters. We develop tools to measure incoherence and characterise when it affects decisions. We introduce the incoherence ratio, an MMD-based measure of how far any updating procedure departs from coherence, computed only from the procedure's own predictions and updates, and accompany it with an anytime-valid test of coherence. In Bayesian experimental design, acquisition objectives that are equivalent for coherent models choose different data under every approximate model we study, and the incoherence ratio tracks how far incoherence distorts them. We also introduce action coherence, which captures only the incoherence that changes a decision. What a resulting disagreement costs, however, is determined primarily by predictive accuracy. Sequential decisions depend on how a model updates as well as on what it predicts, so coherence, like accuracy, should be checked rather than assumed.

papers.title: High-Speed Forward and Reverse Tractor-Trailer Driving with Learned Vehicle Dynamics
papers.abstract: Tractor-trailer systems are difficult to control, especially unstable during reverse motion, and their dynamics depend on difficult-to-measure factors, including road friction and suspension coefficients. We introduce a learned dynamics model for tractor-trailer control and compare it with a reduced-order dynamics model with Fiala tire forces as an analytic baseline. Specifically, we compare a model predictive path integral (MPPI) controller that uses the learned dynamics model to an MPPI controller that uses the analytic model, as well as to three additional baseline controllers. In the main closed-loop tracking experiments across four simulated environments, MPPI with learned dynamics achieves mean speeds closer to the target magnitudes and lower root-mean-square (RMS) hitch angles than MPPI with the analytic model at every tested setpoint, with higher completion rates in seven of eight reverse configurations.

papers.title: Strain-Engineering Giant Pseudo-Electric Fields in Multilayer Graphene
papers.abstract: Electromagnetic scalar and vector potentials can be engineered in solids through lattice distortions, providing a versatile means of tuning electronic band structures. The pseudovector component, which generates pseudo-magnetic fields, has received much attention for its ability to realize a zero-field quantum Hall effect. However, the pseudoscalar component, giving rise to pseudo-electric fields to which many electronic systems are intrinsically susceptible, has not yet been experimentally explored. Here, we demonstrate the emergence and profound consequences of the pseudoscalar potential in a multilayer graphene system. Atomic relaxation reconstructs the system into large Bernalstacked domains separated by one-dimensional rhombohedral channels. Within this inter-dimensional system, we achieve the first direct atomic-scale imaging of distinct lattice deformations in graphene under strain. In rhombohedral channels, we observe that the tensile lattice deformation induces giant pseudo-electric fields, producing ultra-flat dispersion with divergent density of states and a large energy gap. This results in enhanced electronic correlations, leading to flat-band instabilities and striped modulation in the density of states that would otherwise require strong external displacement fields. Moreover, the gap opened by the pseudoscalar potential protects topological boundary states that persist in the absence of applied fields. Our results provide a comprehensive atomic-scale characterization of graphene elasticity and direct spectroscopic evidence for the nontrivial pseudo-electric field arising from lattice distortion. More broadly, it provides an intrinsic and tunable pathway to new quantum states

papers.title: Maximum Scores and Treatment Feedback in Regression Discontinuity Designs
papers.abstract: Hospitals use repeated risk scores to decide when to send an alert. Some evaluations summarize these scores by their maximum and use the maximum as the running variable in a regression discontinuity (RD) design. The maximum shows correctly whether a patient was ever alerted. However, it can include scores recorded after an earlier alert has already changed care. In this paper, we study what the maximum-score RD estimates when an earlier intervention changes a later score. We use a two-assessment model and derive a formula that splits the RD contrast into the causal effect and a composition term. When feedback moves scores in one direction, the composition term equals the relative jump in the density of the maximum at the cutoff times a prognostic contrast. Therefore, an exactly continuous density means no bias, and the population density jump bounds the bias. Valid inference on the jump turns this into a confidence bound under a stated sensitivity assumption. Within this model, bias behind a continuous density requires feedback in both directions. For this case, we bound bias by total boundary movement and construct conservative confidence sets for binary outcomes under explicit sensitivity and smoothness assumptions. We give closed forms for independent uniform scores and for correlated Gaussian scores. In one example, a true risk reduction of four percentage points appears as a one-point increase. Simulations confirm the formulas. Narrower bandwidths, robust bias correction, and machine-learning covariate adjustment do not remove the bias. A fuzzy RD on the first score recovers the causal effect when early and late treatment have the same effect. Our results concern how the running variable is built. We do not assess any published clinical study.

papers.title: Unreasonable Confidence from Simulator Misspecification: Directional Robustness on the SPEED+ Sim-to-Real Benchmark
papers.abstract: Vision-based navigation systems for orbit must be trained almost entirely on synthetic imagery, because real labelled images of a given spacecraft in flight rarely exist. Benchmarks like SPEED+ are built for that situation: the training set comes from a simulator, and the test sets are real images of a satellite mockup under two kinds of lighting. That simulator approximates how light reflects off mylar and aluminium, and like every scientific simulator it is misspecified. Its error is radiometric, since it misses the specular highlights, hard shadows and sensor saturation common in real images. We probe the resulting synthetic-to-real gap, the central risk for such systems, with a deliberately simple monocular pose estimator. In a 2x2 study of backbone adaptation and photometric augmentation, trained on synthetic images and tested on both real hardware-in-the-loop domains, we find three things. (1) The model does not know it is failing: regions conformally calibrated to 90% on synthetic data cover only 9-15% of rotation errors on sunlamp and 21-38% on lightbox, so a wrong pose carries the confidence of a correct one. (2) Transfer is asymmetric: scaling data and features improved synthetic rotation error from 1.65 to 1.03 rad but moved the harshly lit sunlamp domain by only 0.05 rad, under twice its seed s.d., whereas adapting the backbone's last stage carried 63-83% of its extra synthetic gain to both real domains. (3) Once the backbone adapts, augmentation helps only in the direction it models: our photometric stack improved the diffusely lit lightbox domain from 1.17 to 0.99 rad on every seed but moved sunlamp no more than seed-to-seed variation, while with the backbone frozen it helped sunlamp more. Every post-review experiment was pre-registered, and the code, per-image predictions and pre-registration record are at https://github.com/lokindoo/spacecraft-pose-estimation.

papers.title: Course-Referenced Lateral Control of Trail-Following Convoys: String Stability and Adaptive Feedforward under Load Uncertainty
papers.abstract: Vehicles in a convoy can steer along the GNSS trails of the vehicles ahead when lane markings are unavailable, as on snow covered roads. Since each vehicle's tracking error enters the reference of the next, lateral errors can grow along the convoy. This paper presents a course referenced formulation of trail following in arc length, in which each follower takes the direction of its fitted trail as its heading reference. Error propagation then reduces to a single transfer function. We derive a condition under which combining the trails of the leader and the predecessor keeps the errors bounded for any convoy length, and show that following the predecessor alone lets the errors accumulate without bound, even without amplification, on roads that end turned or shifted sideways. Passenger and cargo loads and tire stiffness vary in practice, and we show that they enter the curvature feedforward through a single coefficient, whose mismatch leaves steady offsets on curves. We propose an adaptive law that estimates this coefficient on curves and removes the offsets. Simulations of an eleven vehicle convoy confirm the analysis.

papers.title: How did data sharing evolve in the decade since the FAIR Principles?
papers.abstract: A decade after the publication of the FAIR Guiding Principles, what have we learned about data sharing, and what do data availability statements (DAS) and other materials accrued over that period tell us about how data-sharing practices, attitudes, and infrastructures evolved? Here, we present a large-scale longitudinal analysis of over 6.8 million biomedical articles from the PMC Open Access Subset, spanning 2011 to 2025. Using an automated pipeline, we extracted and classified DAS, repository links, accession numbers, and supplementary materials, assigning each article a data-sharing score and independently FAIR-assessing a subset of cited dataset URLs. We find that explicit DAS adoption rose from ~2% in 2011 to 68% in 2025, while "available on request" statements grew in parallel from near zero to over 19%. The corpus growth amplifies both patterns: articles with a DAS containing an explicit repository mention rose from 132 in 2011 to 94,697 in 2025, while "available on request" articles rose from 77 to 173,474 over this span. Structural biology and genomics consistently achieved the highest data-sharing scores, while clinical research and public health ranked lowest. Gold Open Access journals showed a small advantage over subscription journals, while Diamond Open Access journals outperformed both. Internationally collaborative articles scored higher than domestic ones. A gender gap emerged: female first-authored articles' scores declined more than male first-authored ones. The analysis further covered additional dimensions, from compliance with funder/journal mandates and JATS XML tagging standards to computational reproducibility signals and the co-occurrence of DAS with ethics statements. A decade on, the gap between declaring data availability and actually sharing machine-readable, reusable data persists across fields, infrastructures and demographics.

papers.title: Near-Optimal Methods for Generalized Lipschitz Convex Optimization
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider a convex optimization problem, where the upper bound on the subgradient norm depends on the objective function. We establish a lower bound on the number of iterations required by any first-order method to find an approximate solution to the problem. Furthermore, we present two near-optimal algorithms that can match the lower bound up to logarithmic factors. The first algorithm is a projected GD with a carefully designed stepsize schedule which incorporates warm-up and decay phases. The second algorithm is scalar-stepsize clipped AdamW which extends the near-optimal guarantees to the stochastic setting, where only a noisy unbiased estimator of the subgradient is available.

papers.title: Electronic bridge for the $J=0$ state and effects of electrons on frequency and lifetime of the nuclear clock transition in $^{229}$Th$^{2+}$ ion
papers.abstract: We investigate the electronic bridge (EB) process for excitation of the $^{229}$Th nuclear isomer in Th III ions initially prepared in the metastable electronic state with $J=0$. This state is of particular interest for developing a nuclear clock with suppressed electronic hyperfine interactions. Using a combination of configuration interaction and coupled-cluster methods, we calculate EB transition rates for several excitation schemes involving one or two laser fields. We express the rates in terms of the enhancement factor $R$, defined as the ratio of the EB transition rate to the direct nuclear M1 transition rate. Schemes that return the ion to its initial $J=0$ state have relatively small enhancement factors, $R \sim 1$. However, allowing the final electronic state to differ from the initial state produces a strong resonant enhancement: $R$ reaches $5\times10^3$. In addition, we calculate the shift in the nuclear transition frequency caused by changing the electronic state from the ground state to two excited metastable states. We also examine how the electronic state affects the nuclear transition lifetime and calculate the probabilities of electron transitions induced by nuclear decay. The EB mechanism shortens the nuclear decay lifetime by a factor of 2.6 when the electrons are initially in the ground state and by a factor of 6.85 when they are in the metastable $J=0$ state.

papers.title: Solving the Discretised Shallow Water Equations on Distorted Structured Grids with Neural Physics
papers.abstract: This paper presents a method for solving the shallow water equations on highly distorted structured grids using convolution-based operators following the Neural Physics approach. By mapping distorted physical grids to a uniform computational domain with Jacobian transformations, the governing advection and diffusion operators are reformulated in a structured convolutional form. This enables the use of efficient stencil-based operations and, following the Neural Physics concept, we do this through convolutional layers whose weights are determined by the chosen numerical methods rather than by training. The method introduces consistent mass-lumped formulations, conservative and non-conservative advection forms, and a diffusion operator, all expressed as convolutions. A nonlinear Petrov-Galerkin stabilisation is incorporated to control numerical oscillations on distorted meshes. Two approximations for the Laplacian operator are also proposed to accelerate pressure and diffusion solves. The framework is validated using the Carlisle 2005 flood event, demonstrating accurate predictions of water depth and velocity on distorted meshes for both linear and quadratic discretisations. The results show that distorted structured grids can retain conservation, stability and accuracy, whilst adapting the mesh statically. The convolutional formulation makes the method well suited to Neural Physics implementations and GPU acceleration, offering a scalable approach for flood modelling and large-scale geophysical simulations.

papers.title: Vibe Interventions: Can Users Personalize and Iterate Their Way to Behavior Change?
papers.abstract: Recent advances in large language models allow a working application to be generated from natural-language description, and is referred to as generative user interfaces. Their application to behavior change is unexplored, and we provide one of the first controlled investigations of it. We distinguish two components of authorship: iteration, the revision of a generated artifact in natural language, and personalization, the conditioning of generation on stated context. In a pre-registered between-subjects experiment (N = 300, 60 per condition), we crossed these two factors and added a static intervention as a control, yielding five conditions; participants stated a goal and received a generated intervention. The personalized generative condition ranked highest on every self-report outcome, including ownership, satisfaction, and intended adoption. Randomized iteration had no detectable effect, and higher revision counts were negatively associated with evaluative ratings. This work establishes which component of authorship carries motivational value in generative behavior change tools.

papers.title: NF-VLA: A Normalizing-Flow Baseline for Vision-Language-Action Learning
papers.abstract: Autoregressive normalizing flows (NFs) provide a tractable density for learning and sampling continuous robot actions. We show that a single maximum-likelihood objective can train vision--language--action (VLA) policies competitive with leading methods on manipulation benchmarks. We present NF-VLA, which combines conditional autoregressive normalizing flows with score-based action refinement. Its deep--shallow architecture concentrates visual, language, and proprioceptive prefix conditioning in a high-capacity deep block, while unconditioned shallow blocks provide a shared invertible action transformation. The vision--language backbone and flow are jointly trained by exact maximum likelihood on Gaussian-smoothed action chunks. The same learned density supplies a single score-based correction at inference, refining generated actions to account for training-time smoothing without a separately trained denoiser. Trained on LIBERO from a pretrained vision--language backbone without robot pretraining, NF-VLA achieves 98.35\% success across the four standard suites and 72.6\% on LIBERO-Plus using the same checkpoint without further fine-tuning. Ablations show that deep-only prefix conditioning and score-based refinement both improve closed-loop success. Together, these results establish carefully structured autoregressive flows as a competitive approach to VLA control, with one learned density supporting policy training, action generation, and refinement.

papers.title: Generalized Rotating-Wave Approximations Hierarchy for the Interacting Two-Qubit Rabi Model
papers.abstract: We investigate the two-qubit quantum Rabi model for identical qubits symmetrically coupled to a single bosonic mode and interacting with each other through transverse and longitudinal couplings. We extend the adiabatic, generalized rotating-wave (GRWA), and squeezed generalized rotating-wave (SGRWA) approximations to include the qubit-qubit interactions, including self-consistent and variational choices of the bosonic parameters. The resulting analytical hierarchy allows us to distinguish the interplay between both kinds of qubit-qubit interactions and the effects of displacement, neighboring-manifold mixing, and squeezing on the low-energy properties. We find that the transverse interaction mainly changes the collective-spin structure of the states, while the longitudinal interaction also modifies the displacement-dependent oscillator overlaps and introduces an additional two-boson coupling. We compare the analytical results with numerically exact diagonalization for the low-energy spectrum, ground-state energy, mean photon number, two-qubit concurrence, and spin correlations. The results provide a compact analytical description of how direct qubit-qubit interactions modify both the spectrum and the eigenstate structure beyond the rotating-wave approximation for few-qubit light-matter systems.

papers.title: Soft-constrained Schrödinger bridge for generative AI: numerical algorithms and approximation guarantees
papers.abstract: We study a soft-constrained formulation of the Schrödinger bridge problem, in which the terminal distribution constraint is relaxed into a penalty on the discrepancy between the terminal law of the controlled process and a target distribution. This leads to an unconstrained McKean--Vlasov stochastic control problem, where the interaction enters only through the terminal cost. We characterize the optimizer via a McKean--Vlasov forward-backward stochastic differential equation and establish well-posedness under very mild assumptions. We also analyze two approximation regimes relevant to data-driven computation: approximation of the target law by empirical samples, and finite-particle approximation of the McKean--Vlasov control problem. For both, we derive convergence results and error estimates. Finally, building on the well-posedness and approximation results, we investigate two neural numerical methods: one based on the forward-backward system and the other on direct control optimization. Both methods are tested on state-of-the-art generative tasks. Our results provide both an algorithmic foundation and its theoretical guarentee for soft-constrained Schrödinger bridge problems in sample-based generative modeling.

papers.title: Reveal: A Provenance-Aware System for Multimodal Urban Data Exploration
papers.abstract: Urban sensing initiatives increasingly produce multimodal datasets that combine visual and textual information to capture city characteristics and subjective factors such as safety, comfort, and accessibility. Yet, analyzing such data at scale remains difficult, as manual inspection is unfeasible and automated methods struggle to interpret subjective cues and uncover relationships across diverse data modalities. Moreover, existing workflows rarely make exploration steps explicit, hindering reproducibility. To address these challenges, we introduce Reveal, a provenance-aware visual analytics system for exploring heterogeneous urban data. Reveal enables users to build dataflows by combining text and image searches across coordinated views, chaining queries into pipelines, and applying set operations within an exploration diagram while capturing analytical provenance. We evaluate Reveal through two case studies focused on accessibility and walkability.

papers.title: Strengthening Compact Vehicle Routing Formulations through Arc-Flow Aggregation and Refinement
papers.abstract: Arc-flow formulations can provide strong relaxations for mixed-integer program formulations of vehicle routing problems, but the associated networks may be prohibitively large. We study the setting in which multiple arc flow relaxations may be applied, and introduce a dual-guided aggregation and refinement framework that constructs substantially smaller arc-flow formulations while recovering the LP bound of the original networks. Dual information is used both to identify states that can be aggregated without weakening the bound and to guide node disaggregation. We show that the resulting procedure converges finitely to the arc-flow bound of the full arc-flow formulation. The framework retains the original decision variables, allowing cutting planes to be added directly in the original variable space. Moreover, it produces an explicit MILP formulation without relying on column generation or pricing to determine the arc-flow relaxation bound. We apply our approach to the vehicle routing problem with time windows for which we define two arc flow relaxations, as well as two families of cutting planes over the original variable space. Computational experiments show that strong bounds can be obtained using substantially aggregated networks. The resulting root bounds are competitive with those obtained by the branch-and-price solver RouteOpt, while retaining a formulation that can be solved directly by a general-purpose MILP solver.

papers.title: Graph spectra and late-time concurrence in a lossy reservoir network
papers.abstract: We investigate how coupling the local environments of noninteracting qubits into a network changes their late-time entanglement dynamics. Each qubit interacts with a lossy bosonic memory mode, with coherent hopping between memory modes determined by an underlying graph. The initial state contains at most two excitations. We show that the graph spectrum selects the collective modes that survive longest, thereby controlling both the decay and spatial distribution of pair concurrence. At resonance, nonbipartite graphs generically approach a fixed pattern of relative concurrence determined by the Perron eigenvector, whereas bipartite graphs support interference between two equally damped modes. This interference can produce arbitrarily late entanglement revivals when it overcomes the exponential decay of the surviving modes. We derive explicit thresholds separating revival and eventual monotonic decay, and show that loss from two-excitation states can drive the system across these thresholds without changing the graph or the initial one-excitation state. Underlying these results is a general bound on the sector decay rates, $γ_2\ge2γ_1$, valid at arbitrary uniform detuning. We also identify an exceptional equal-rate regime in which coherence between the vacuum and two-excitation sectors contributes to the leading concurrence. Together, these results establish how the topology of a structured dissipative environment and the redistribution of excitations through loss determine the long-time behavior of entanglement.

papers.title: Stability conditions on Lazarsfeld-Mukai bundles over abelian surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the stability of Lazarsfeld-Mukai bundles associated with smooth curves over abelian surfaces. When the general curve in $|L|$ have Clifford dimension one and maximal gonality, for $ρ\gg 0$ we show that every component of the relative Brill-Noether loci \(W^1_d(|L|)\) dominating the linear system parametrizes generically \(μ_L\)-stable rank-two Lazarsfeld-Mukai bundles. We also apply Bayer-Li wall-crossing to higher-rank bundles: if \(\operatorname{NS}(S)=\mathbb Z\cdot L\), \(A\) is a globally generated complete linear series of degree \(d\) on a smooth curve \(C\in|L|\), \(h^0(C,A)=r+1\) with \(r>2\), and \(d\ne g-1\), then the associated bundle \(E_{C,A}\) is \(μ_L\)-stable and \(L\)-Gieseker-stable. The corresponding object \(E_{C,A}^{\vee}[1]\) for \(d<g-1\), or \(E_{C,A}\) for \(d>g-1\), is stable in the adjacent chamber, as its reduction. These results connect dimension estimates for Brill-Noether loci with stability and wall-crossing on abelian surfaces.

papers.title: PoCoAttn: Position-Content Collaborative Sparse Attention for Fast and High-Fidelity Video Generation
papers.abstract: Video diffusion transformers rely on 3D full attention over tens of thousands of spatiotemporal tokens, and its quadratic cost dominates inference latency. Sparse attention reduces this cost, but existing methods face a dilemma: static methods apply predefined masks and cannot capture input-dependent attention, whereas dynamic methods reconstruct the sparse mask repeatedly, paying online to rediscover positional structure that is largely stable across inputs. To this end, we propose PoCoAttn, a training-free sparse attention framework that separates input-stable from input-dependent attention and resolves the former offline and the latter online. PoCoAttn features: (1) A relative-offset analysis of 3D query-key pairs, which shows that video attention decomposes into an input-stable positional prior that carries most of the attention mass and a small content-dependent residual. (2) A position-content collaborative sparse attention mechanism, which retrieves positional keys from offline-calibrated tables, selects content keys online with a head-adaptive ratio between the two sources, and compensates for the discarded keys to approximate full attention. (3) A step-adaptive budget allocation algorithm, which models how early-step sparse attention errors are amplified along the denoising trajectory and derives the optimal sparsity budget per step. Extensive experiments across four video diffusion models and three tasks show that PoCoAttn consistently achieves a better speed-fidelity Pareto frontier than state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods, improving PSNR by 1.9 to 5.0 dB over baselines and delivering up to 4.1$\times$ attention and 2.0$\times$ denoising speedups over dense FlashAttention-3 attention.

papers.title: Ontology-Compiled Control Barrier Functions for Heterogeneous Robot Teams
papers.abstract: Safety filters for heterogeneous robot teams fail because of missing constraints, overestimated braking capabilities and conflicts between individually satisfiable constraints. We present OntoCBF, which compiles a domain ontology with a class taxonomy, typed relations, safety axioms and a dynamics profile per robot class into a control barrier function filter with one quadratic program per agent. Description-logic entailment supplies the constraints of any team online, including those that follow from chains of relations and from classes defined by what a robot carries, so the existing safety axioms cover new robot classes, payload classes and combinations. We prove that a subclass may reuse the braking capability of its parent whenever it can produce every velocity of the parent, a property separate from subsumption. For box-bounded double integrators this property is also necessary, and every loss of safety then begins with a conflict. Once three robots interact, the safe set of pairwise barriers contains states from which a collision is unavoidable, and such states persist in larger teams under any fixed capability reduction. In a simulated warehouse where humans ignore the robots, a filter written for the design classes violates safety in 89-100 % of the episodes with unseen classes. In all scenarios, including one with 32 robots, OntoCBF violates safety in 20-70 % of the episodes, each time after a conflict, with a median deepest intrusion of 10-17 % of the keep-out distance. A multi-agent PPO policy trained with the filter in the loop lowers the rate of infeasible quadratic programs, nearly all of them conflicts, by 18-41 %.

papers.title: Hochschild Cocycle and Universality of Merge
papers.abstract: The Hopf algebra Markov chain dynamical system, on the Hopf algebra of non-planar binary forests, that models the action of Merge on workspaces in Chomsky's Minimalist Model of syntax, satisfies a universal property, determined by the fact that the Merge operation is a Hochschild 1-cocycle. This universal property has an interpretation in terms of models of the syntax-semantics interface, as it shows that, if the side of semantics possesses a sufficiently rich compositional structure, then that structure is uniquely induced by the syntactic Merge, once the semantic values of lexical items and syntactic features are assigned. We illustrate how this universality works by showing, in particular, full compatibility of this Hopf algebraic formulation with Heim-Kratzer semantics.

papers.title: A notion of pseudo-morphisms with applications to the study of polynomial maps and of link-homotopy groups of 2-string link
papers.abstract: We introduce a notion of pseudo-morphism for groups, which extends the notion of group morphism from a group to a ring. We show that pseudo-morphisms from a group $G$ to an integral domain $R$ form a filtred Hopf algebra which can be seen as an efficient notion of dual for $G$. We also show that pseudo-morphisms are closely related to the notion of polynomial maps in the sense of Eilenberg-MacLane/Passi, the two notions even coinciding when $G$ is finitely generated and $R$ is a field. It follows that, in that case, polynomial maps are endowed with an Hopf structure. In a second part, we study non repeated Milnor invariants (in the $4$-dimensional context of $2$-string links) from this pseudo-morphism point of view. We show that they form a sub-bialgebra of the Hopf algebra of pseudo-morphisms on the group of $2$-string links up to link-homotopy, and prove that it is isomorphic to an explicit quotient $\textrm{Mil}$ of a polynomial ring. This leads to a fully algebraic description of the group of 2-string links up to link-homotopy as the dual group associated to $\textrm{Mil}$. As a by-product, we obtain that non repeated Milnor invariants are polynomial maps, and we show that this can be used to give a new proof of their finite type property.

papers.title: On dynamical and parameter spaces for the Maximally Generalized McMullen family of rational maps
papers.abstract: We explore the maximally generalized McMullen family of rational maps $F_{n,d,c,a}(z) = z^n + a/z^d + c$, for $n,d\in \mathbb{Z},$ with $n,d\geq 3$, $a\in \mathbb{C}^*$ and $c\in \mathbb{C}$. In the dynamical plane, we establish annular regions containing the Julia sets, and show that the geometric limits of both the Julia and filled Julia sets as $n,d\to \infty$ are contained in the unit circle. In parameter space, for any fixed $a\in \mathbb{C}^*$, we examine the boundedness locus in the $c$-plane. When $n=d$ we find that as $n\to \infty$, the boundedness locus tends to the union of two unit circles centered at $\pm 2\sqrt{a}$. For arbitrary $n,d$, we identify a spine consisting of unit circles determined by the critical values, and prove that the boundedness locus tends to the spine as $n,d\to \infty$.

papers.title: Population structure of the velocity distribution in normal shock waves: Gaussian representations, Mach-number similarity, and prediction
papers.abstract: Normal shock waves are commonly described as mixtures of upstream and downstream Maxwellians. Discrete-velocity solutions of three relaxation models up to Mach 12 and direct simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) of hard-sphere and variable-hard-sphere gases up to Mach 25 are used to examine the population structure, Mach-number similarity and upstream precursor of their velocity distributions. Three anisotropic Gaussian populations reproduce the streamwise reduced distributions of the Bhatnagar--Gross--Krook (BGK) model and of DSMC to within 4\% up to Mach 12, and of DSMC to within 6\% at Mach 25, whereas two Maxwellians incur errors up to 50\% (BGK) and 37\% (DSMC). Collision histories identify the hard-sphere beam with unscattered stream molecules, which carry half of the peak viscous stress; the other populations are effective descriptions, not collision classes. Above Mach 5, Rankine--Hugoniot-scaled distributions are nearly Mach-independent, with corrections linear in $1/M^2$, consistent with the scaled kinetic equation. At equal normalised density, Mach 8 and 12 give the heat flux and stress at Mach 25 within 1\%, comparable to the accuracy of the reference; with one moment equation for position, physical-space profiles follow within 5\%. Comparing three prediction methods shows that the accuracy comes from the scaling; the Gaussian form adds compactness. Ahead of the shock, the mass of upstream-moving molecules decays as a stretched exponential with effective exponent 0.68--0.87. Collisions regenerate upstream-moving molecules, which explains a decay slower than free-flight survival; a linear cascade model with a downstream-Maxwellian source and no input from the shock interior reproduces the decay rates within 1.2\%.

papers.title: Multi-output neural network surrogate for double-pulse femtosecond optothermal control of thin silicon films on fused silica
papers.abstract: We introduce a multi-output feedforward neural network surrogate trained on a coupled multiple-reflection and two-temperature model to map double-pulse femtosecond laser excitation (1030 nm) of crystalline silicon films on fused silica across film thicknesses (50-500 nm) and inter-pulse delays (0-10ps). Trained via Levenberg-Marquardt optimization on 2000 physical simulations, the dual-hidden-layer network ([40,30] neurons) simultaneously predicts six strongly coupled optothermal observables, peak electron temperature, peak lattice temperature, peak carrier density, minimum and maximum absorptivity and minimum refractive index achieving coefficients of determination R2 larger than 0.9998 across all targets. Evaluating a dense 200 by 200 design grid in milliseconds resolves pronounced thin-film interference fringes and carrier-induced index modulation, identifying an optimal optothermal coupling regime at d=156 nm and Dt=4.572 ps. This unified machine-learning workflow eliminates computationally expensive multi-physics runtime bottlenecks for real-time laser processing control and inverse photonic thin-film design.

papers.title: Faster $χ^2$ periodogram: Accelerating linear algebra with fast Toeplitz solvers
papers.abstract: In recent years, the traditional Lomb--Scargle periodogram, relying on least-squares fitting of a sinusoid to data with a known mean, has been mostly superseded by its floating-mean extension---the generalized Lomb--Scargle periodogram---due to the superior robustness and accuracy of the latter. While further generalization to higher-degree trigonometric polynomials (known as the multiharmonic analysis of variance and the fast $χ^2$ periodogram) has been known for decades, its usage remains relatively uncommon, mostly due to its significantly higher computational cost. Here we present a technique reducing the computational complexity of such an extension by combining a Toeplitz formulation of the system of normal equations with non-uniform fast Fourier transforms, coupled with condition-number monitoring to protect against numerical instability. When modified for practical efficiency rather than asymptotic computational complexity, our approach reaches speed-ups exceeding an order of magnitude over current state-of-the-art implementations across a wide range of hyperparameters when evaluated on multithreaded systems, while matching or exceeding their accuracy. Additionally, we provide a reference implementation used for benchmarking, along with the code used to generate the results presented in this work.

papers.title: On cover exacting cardinals
papers.abstract: We answer a question of Goldberg about cover exacting cardinals. Concretely, we show that if $κ$ is $ω_1$-strongly compact, then no cardinal $λ>κ$ is $γ$-cover exacting for some cardinal $γ$.

papers.title: Type-Confusion Security
papers.abstract: Type systems are a lightweight way to obtain formal assurance that code upholds security properties. However, decentralized systems, such as smart contracts and Model Context Protocol ecosystems, have limited ability to constrain the behavior of untrusted code. In such systems, attackers may attempt to confuse trusted code by supplying values that do not behave according to their advertised types, an attack that we call type confusion. Well-known attacks such as confused deputy attacks, reentrancy attacks, and control-flow hijacking can be understood as instances of type confusion. We define type confusion security as the property that unrestricted attackers who need not follow the type system have no more power than limited attackers who fully obey it. We formally define type confusion security as a real--ideal emulation, and in the context of an information-flow-typed core calculus that statically enforces security against well-typed attackers, prove that its run-time checks also enforce security against ill-typed attackers. In this system, programmers can write code while reasoning about security only against well-typed attackers; the security guarantees enforced by the type system still hold. We mechanize a proof of type confusion security in Lean.

papers.title: Reliable Mining of Heterogeneous AI Coding-Agent Data: Context-Aware Prediction and Resource-Aware Ranking
papers.abstract: Operational records from AI coding agents differ across agents, repositories, tasks, and workflows. We study 71,677 pull requests (PRs) from six agents and show that pooling these records can reverse descriptive and predictive conclusions. PRs carrying a co-authorship trailer have a 55.6% merge rate, compared with 77.5% without the trailer, but removing the dominant agent flips this -21.8 percentage-point gap to +23.7 points. We treat this Simpson-type reversal as a data-veracity problem and represent source, environment, and workflow context in a feature cascade. Gradient-boosting merge-prediction AUC increases from 0.774 to 0.832; the advantage persists under temporal evaluation (0.801) and unseen repositories (0.807). The co-authorship coefficient changes from -1.09 to +1.44 after conditioning, whereas repository-clustered AIPW intervals show no stable adjusted trailer association. A strict PR-creation-time model reaches 0.741 AUC in standard evaluation and 0.710 on unseen repositories, although its temporal AUC falls to 0.641. Finally, a separately cross-fitted analysis of an observed-mode functional estimates a +12.3-point doubly robust gain at a 30% allocation budget on the non-Codex population, only 0.5 points above risk ranking. This last result is retrospective decision support over metadata states, not a causal effect of assigning human review.

papers.title: Descending Everest, Part III: Oracle Complexity of Monotone Variational Inequalities with $(L_0,L_1)$-Lipschitz Operators
papers.abstract: We consider monotone variational inequalities in which the Jacobian norm of the operator $F:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d$ is bounded by an affine function of the norm of the operator itself: $\|DF(z)\|\le L_0+L_1\|F(z)\|$. The main case is the problem on the whole space, that is, finding a zero of $F$. We assume that a solution exists and that an upper bound $R$ on the distance from the starting point to the solution is known. Neither strong monotonicity nor cocoercivity is assumed. Global Lipschitz continuity is not assumed either: for $L_1>0$, the Jacobian norm may grow together with the norm of the operator. We obtain upper and lower bounds on the number of oracle calls sufficient to find a point $\hat z$ with $\|F(\hat z)\|\le\varepsilon$. For $L_0R/\varepsilon\ge1$, both bounds are, up to logarithmic factors in $L_1R$, of order $1+L_0R/\varepsilon+(L_1R)^{6/5}$. The upper bound is attained by a deterministic extragradient-type method, and the lower bound holds for arbitrary randomized methods. The same bounds are obtained for the Minty gap on the ball of radius $R$, where $L_0R/\varepsilon$ is replaced by $L_0R^2/η$. In addition, we show that for a variational inequality on a bounded set the numbers $L_0,L_1$ and the diameter of the set are not sufficient: a uniform complexity bound requires additional information, for example, an upper bound on the norm of the operator at the solution.

papers.title: Off-shell one-loop counterterms of Palatini gravity with an independent background connection
papers.abstract: We compute the one-loop divergences of pure gravity in the first-order (Palatini) formulation, using the background field method in Goldberg variables, with a background connection independent of the background metric. Background Ward-Takahashi identities are verified at one loop. The divergences of the two-point functions, obtained in arbitrary dimension and gauge, require, besides the curvature-squared terms, invariants built from the nonmetricity of the background connection; in particular, the Gauss-Bonnet combination, which is not topological for a nonmetric connection, does not suffice. Three- and four-point functions in the Feynman-de Donder gauge complete the counterterm Lagrangian up to fourth order in the nonmetricity and provide parameter-free tests of it. All the counterterms vanish on shell, as in the metric formulation, and off shell they can be removed by field redefinitions.

papers.title: "God says we are right!": The Interplay between Religion and Propaganda on Arabic Social Media
papers.abstract: Religion is a main aspect of life in many parts of the world; hence, it acts as a powerful tool for influencing people's views and actions. In the context of propaganda and misinformation, religion has been perceived as a factor that impacts people negatively leading them to be influenced by false or biased information. However, there are limited quantitative studies that explore the exact role of religion in this process. In this study, we investigate whether state-sponsored propaganda accounts share religious content in a different way than the typical norms reported in the literature and whether they mobilize this content to promote their agendas. This is achieved by exploring 15 Middle Eastern propaganda Twitter datasets encompassing around 124 million tweets from 32.5K accounts attributed to KSA, UAE, Egypt, Turkey, and Iran. We find that propagandists share excerpts from the Quran and Hadith according to patterns that reflect aspects of their state's agenda. We also demonstrate examples where such religious texts were used to modulate political messages.

papers.title: Model-Free Stealthy Attack on Vehicle Systems and Its Implications for ISO/SAE 21434 Risk Assessment
papers.abstract: This paper investigates a model-free stealthy adversary targeting in-vehicle networks and its implications for automotive cybersecurity risk assessment. Conventional stealthy false-data-injection (FDI) attacks often assume privileged knowledge of system dynamics, estimator parameters, or detector statistics, understating the feasibility of adversaries with limited system information. We develop a model-free FDI attack that uses a Vector Autoregressive model with Exogenous inputs (VARX), identified from passively recorded nominal measurements, to characterize a compromised channel and construct attack sequences within a data-calibrated residual envelope. The construction requires no vehicle dynamics model, estimator parameters, assumed noise distribution, or detector knowledge. In a closed-loop lane-keeping benchmark, the attack induces a 1.25 m lateral displacement, exceeding the specified 0.9 m half-lane width, and keeps the vehicle outside the lane corridor for 9.21 s. At a matched 1 % false-alarm operating point, attack-period alarm rates stay below 2.4 % across five learning-based intrusion detection systems (IDSs), a chi-squared residual monitor, and a liveness monitor, versus 66-100 % for conventional baselines. The proposed adversary matches the impact and evasion of a privileged model-based adversary while requiring 13 fewer attack-potential points, raising its assessed feasibility from Low to High under the considered ISO/SAE 21434 Threat Analysis and Risk Assessment (TARA). We further show that conventional impact-and-feasibility risk scoring can assign identical risk to attacks with substantially different detector responses, and introduce a detection-conditioned risk formulation to distinguish them. These findings highlight the importance of accounting for adversarial knowledge requirements and measured detectability when assessing risks in safety-critical vehicle systems.

papers.title: Causal Discovery for Resiliency-Prioritized Transmission Expansion Planning in Power Systems with Grid-Forming Inverter-Based Resources
papers.abstract: Transmission planners at regional transmission organizations (RTOs), independent system operators (ISOs), and NERC-registered entities have limited analytical resources for exploring expansion options that improve resiliency for withstanding and recovering from fault conditions in electric power systems that are dominated by grid-forming (GFM) and grid-following (GFL) inverter-based resources (IBRs). Conventional existing TPL-001 contingency analysis will assess if a performance benchmark is violated. However, it will not identify which dynamic states and inputs caused the violation, nor how much a protective action will avoid propagation into a cascading outage. This paper proposes an analytical method that combines time-series causal discovery using the Peter and Clark Momentary Conditional Independence (PCMCI) algorithm with right/left eigenvector participation-factor analysis of validated small-signal state-space models. Synthetic data are generated from linearized models derived from substation phasor measurement unit (PMU) data. This includes node-breaker topologies under alternative transmission switching configurations. GFM and GFL inverter controls including phase-locked loops (PLLs) and fault ride-through logic. A planning index referred to as the Resiliency Causal Contribution Index (RCCI) is defined that weights PCMCI-derived causal effects on a TPL benchmark quantity by modal participation. The planning procedure iterates contingency categories, measures margins to RTO/ISO benchmarks for transient voltage recovery, oscillatory damping, inverter ride-through, and TPL-008-1 extreme temperature. The process infers automatic protective actions and repeats until a cascade is ruled out or confirmed. A simplified case study illustrates the entire process for considering the options in transmission expansion planning.

papers.title: Where the Savings Go: The Limits of Hiding Cross-Tenant Cache Hits in LLM Serving
papers.abstract: LLM serving engines cache prompt prefixes; a cache hit skips computation and returns faster, so a shared cache reveals whether others have sent a given text. Per-account salting closes this channel but forgoes cross-tenant reuse and isolates only whole accounts, even where access is redistributed or trust domains are subdivided below them. Defenses that share globally but hide hits promise reuse without relying on account boundaries. Hiding a hit requires everything tenants observe afterwards to be distributed as if it had missed. The defenses we examine target the hit-miss gap; we instead follow where the saved time goes. Step-based schedulers that never idle while work waits pass it in full to every request queued behind the hit, shifting each earlier by the same amount. An attacker within ordinary rate limits brackets a probe with two groups of listeners that each return one token, sends them in one short burst, and counts in how many steps they finish. Replaying a production trace on one vLLM instance at up to half capacity, a single probe detects cached texts of 256 tokens or more with advantage at least 0.98. Hiding only the hit request falls to one probe on vLLM and SGLang; random delays must reach about ten times the shift or more to cut the advantage to 0.1; narrowing what is shared gives no guarantee against this inference. Since any observable tenant benefit is also a signal, we prove that a rate-limited tenant's gain from content written by k other accounts is at most of order k times the leakage allowed, whatever the provider does with identities; at zero leakage, only the provider keeps the savings. Exact hiding is attainable in principle on one instance, but mechanisms that only pause or hold work know skipped work's duration only approximately, so under saturated prefill they must pad every step that may hold a hit, at a price that grows with time rather than with hits.

papers.title: Geometric tracking of a halo CME using full-circle wide-field views from PUNCH
papers.abstract: We tracked the large, geoeffective halo coronal mass ejection (CME) of 2025-May-31 across the very wide field of view of the Polarimeter to Unify the Corona and Heliosphere (PUNCH) mission, as a proof of concept for data-informed forecasting of CME arrival times at Earth. using simple point-and-click measurement of the front location as far as 47 degrees away from the Sun itself, we constrained an analytic "ludicrous ice-cream cone" geometric model with just three parameters: position angle, off-Earth-Sun angle, and propagation speed. We show that the model is sufficient to capture the bulk envelope of the CME, and also insufficient to capture the complexity of the CME's evolution. We generated simulated arrival-time forecasts for the CME by extrapolating the constant-velocity propagation to determine the time of impact with Earth. These "retro-forecasts" converged to within 30 +/- 15 minutes of the actual arrival time, 8 hours prior to arrival. The convergence was marked by a clear inflection point in the curve of predicted-arrival-time vs time-of-forecast. We conclude that continuous wide-field tracking is sufficiently powerful to enable even crude models to substantially improve arrival-time forecasting precision, and discuss future work required both to validate this single-event result and to extend it to more sophisticated analyses.

papers.title: Benchmarking LLM Inference on Desktop-Scale NVIDIA Grace Blackwell Clusters
papers.abstract: Two NVIDIA DGX Spark GB10 systems connect directly over 200 GbE to serve larger language models and increase inference capacity, but the benefits depend on how they are deployed. We benchmark 17 open-weight checkpoints spanning dense and mixture-of-experts architectures, 8B to 235B parameters and four weight precisions on one and two RDMA-connected systems. Using vLLM, we compare tensor parallelism (TP=2), pipeline parallelism (PP=2) and a two-replica baseline at concurrency 1 to 64, with three independent launches per configuration. TP=2 delivers a median 1.59x peak-throughput gain over one Spark, versus 1.39x for PP=2 and has higher throughput in 93 of 96 matched comparisons with separated 95% Welch intervals. It reduces unloaded inter-token latency to 0.52x to 0.73x of one Spark, whereas PP=2 provides little reduction. TP=2 also achieves the highest goodput under a strict 100 ms inter-token latency objective wherever both strategies are supported and the objective is met. For models fitting on one Spark, TP=2 generally favors low-concurrency serving, while replication offers higher throughput at high concurrency. One Spark uses less GPU energy per output token at matched concurrency. Across three precision ladders, NVFP4 reduces unloaded latency more than adding a second Spark at BF16. NCCL microbenchmarks and comparisons with an earlier TCP campaign suggest that collective communication overhead contributes to the advantage of TP=2. These results provide deployment guidance for desktop-scale inference.

papers.title: Protecting Safety during Reasoning Training with Low-Rank Fisher Regularisation
papers.abstract: Large language models are trained to have safety guardrails, but these can be compromised while fine-tuning for new capabilities, such as reasoning. One way to mitigate this degradation is to modify the fine-tuning objective to preserve safety behaviour, but doing so effectively and efficiently remains challenging. We revisit Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC), which penalises parameter updates based on sensitivity estimates from the diagonal of the Fisher information matrix (FIM). While EWC provides some protection, the diagonal approximation ignores interactions between parameters. We address this limitation by exploiting recent findings that safety-relevant behaviour is located in a low-rank subspace within models. Our method, Subspace-Projected Elastic Weight Consolidation (SP-EWC), projects gradients onto this subspace to capture non-diagonal curvature efficiently. We investigate three different ways of identifying the safety subspace: through safety fine-tuning updates (LoRA), safety-related activations (ActSVD), and contrastive representations of safety and utility data (cPCA). We find that this choice substantially affects performance, with SP-EWC using cPCA comparing favourably against existing methods by better maintaining safety guardrails without introducing excessive over-refusal.

papers.title: Structural properties of semi-cutting sets
papers.abstract: Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple undirected graph, let $T\subseteq V$, and let $F\subseteq E$. We call $F$ semi-cutting for $T$ if $d_{G}(u,w)<d_{G\setminus F}(u,w)$ for every two distinct terminals $u,w\in T$. We prove the sharp bound $|F|\ge |T|-1$. The argument is structural: semi-cutting sets are first identified with edge transversals of all shortest terminal-terminal paths, and the bound then follows from a contraction step, a terminal-deletion lemma, and a lexicographic induction on $(|T|,|V|)$.

papers.title: Maximum likelihood degrees of 3D polytopes built from polygons of ML degree one
papers.abstract: We construct 3D polytopes that admit a scaling with maximum likelihood (ML) degree one by using codimension zero toric fiber products of lower-dimensional polytopes and classify all the 3D polytopes that can be constructed in this way. We also study a family of 3D polytopes whose faces admit ML degree one scalings. We give a tight lower bound for the ML degree of these polytopes with a square base and we show that every value between this bound and the normalized volume of the polytope can be attained. These values depend on counting common and repeated roots associated to certain univariate polynomials. This is similar in spirit to the description of the possible ML degrees of rational normal scrolls.

papers.title: Characterizing nonlocal Sobolev spaces as generalized Bessel potential spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study nonlocal Sobolev spaces $H^{ρ,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ with $p \in (1,\infty)$, defined via a general class of nonlocal gradients $D^ρ$ associated with a kernel function $ρ$. As our main contribution, we establish three new equivalent characterizations of these spaces. First, we describe $H^{ρ,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ in terms of Fourier multipliers involving the symbol of the nonlocal potential associated with $D^ρ$. Second, we give a thorough functional analytic treatment of the nonlocal $ρ$-Laplacian $Δ^ρ$, which allows us to represent general nonlocal Sobolev spaces through its square root $(-Δ^ρ)^{1/2}$. Third, we show that $H^{ρ,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ coincides with the image $g_ρ* L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for a suitable convolution kernel $g_ρ\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^n)$, which confirms that these spaces are genuine potential spaces. These results generalize the well-known fact that, in the special case of the Riesz kernel, the resulting fractional Sobolev spaces coincide with the classical Bessel potential spaces. In this spirit, the present work can also be viewed as introducing a natural notion of generalized Bessel potential spaces.

papers.title: Multi-seed information diffusion with varying reproduction
papers.abstract: We define the $S_hR_k$-process that generalizes the notion of Hamiltonicity through the lense of information diffusion. We say that a graph is $S_hR_k$-infectable if it can be fully infected by transmission trees seeded by at most $h$ initial infections in which each infection leads to at most $k$ others; or, equivalently, if it can be exactly vertex-covered by at most $h$ trees of degree at most $k$. While determining $S_hR_k$ infectability is NP-hard in general, we argue fixed-parameter tractability when parameterised by treewidth. Additionally, we give computational experimental results comparing the performance of several natural heuristics for minimising the number of initial infections required to an optimal LP-based approach on several standard complex network models. We find that a uniformly random approach outperforms greedy heuristics based on degree or clustering.

papers.title: CiGS: Conduction in Gaussian Splats for Interior Temperature Field from Thermal Images
papers.abstract: We present a method for inferring the interior temperature distribution of a solid object from registered multi-view visible-spectrum and thermal images, even when the thermal views cover only part of its surface. We formulate steady-state heat conduction as a Laplace boundary value problem and solve it with a direct boundary integral equation discretized over a point cloud: a Gaussian reconstruction of the visible-spectrum images supplies the boundary geometry, and the thermal images supply the boundary data. We do not build surface or volume meshes at any stage in our method. Instead, we sample collocation points from rendered depth without the pixels at depth discontinuities, and use a density subtraction that keeps the interior evaluation accurate up to the surface. The whole chain is differentiable, and we use it to recover the pose and depth of heating pipes, insulation defects, and the shape of cracks from thermal images. We validate our method through experiments on boundary value problems with Dirichlet-only and mixed Dirichlet and Robin boundaries, using synthetic and real captured data on scenes with challenging topology. These experiments show that our method matches analytical solutions and has better accuracy than FEM solvers.

papers.title: Canonical metrics on punctured spheres, II: compactified moduli spaces of black holes
papers.abstract: Let $g_{\mathfrak{p}_{\ell}}$ denote the canonical scalar-flat metric on $S^n\setminus \mathfrak{p}_{\ell}$ introduced in Part~I, which for $n=3$ corresponds to the Brill--Lindquist initial data for $\ell$ black holes, and let $η\in H_{\ell}$ be its associated mass matrix. In this paper, we investigate the asymptotic behavior of the metrics and the mass matrix $η$ as subsets of punctures collide. Such collisions cause every mass to diverge; if a cluster $A$ of black holes collapses at a relative scale $t$, the mass matrix satisfies $η=E(A)\ln(1/t)+O(1)$, diverging along an explicit ray $E(A)\in H_{\ell}$. For nested families of clusters, this degeneracy structure naturally organizes into a space of rooted trees. Subtracting the divergence gives a renormalized mass matrix which extends smoothly to every stratum of the Axelrod--Singer compactified moduli space $\overline{M}{}^{\,\mathrm{AS}}_\ell= \overline C_{\ell-1}(\mathbb{R}^n)/\mathrm O(n)$ and splits naturally into one mass matrix per vertex of the bubble tree. Geometrically, at each vertex carrying punctures the suitably rescaled metrics converge to a complete scalar-flat metric with the nodes filled in, adjacent such pieces being joined by Schwarzschild necks, and the renormalized matrix acting as its mass data. For $n=3$, the necks contain minimal spheres, which are common apparent horizons of the merging holes. At vertices bearing two holes, we determine on which side of the limiting horizon each node lies, and we formulate as a conjecture the resulting criterion for a neck to be a component of the outermost horizon. We also compare the mass lower bound of Part~I with the Riemannian Penrose inequality. Because the mass matrix is invariant under rotations of the bubbles, it lives on a Deligne--Mumford-type quotient of the compactification.

papers.title: Resolvent-based modeling of turbulent flow over multilayer compliant surfaces
papers.abstract: Compliant coatings offer a passive approach to modifying near-wall turbulence and potentially reducing skin-friction drag, but high-fidelity exploration of the coupled parameter space is costly. We develop a two-way coupled resolvent-Galerkin framework for turbulent channel flow over finite-thickness, layered viscoelastic coatings. The fluid is modeled using the Navier-Stokes equations linearized about a turbulent mean state, while the solid is represented by a through-thickness Galerkin discretization of the elastodynamic equations. The solid response is condensed into a spectral surface-impedance operator at the fluid-solid interface. At $Re_τ= 180$, stiff panels approach the rigid-wall response, whereas more compliant panels modify the low-rank response associated with the near-wall cycle. A Reynolds-number study shows that panels with fixed nondimensional material stiffness can produce different responses depending on whether their thickness scales with inner or outer flow length scales. The influence of viscoelastic damping is examined across low- and high-frequency regimes, where stiffness-proportional damping alters the high-frequency fractional-energy distribution, while the low-frequency distribution remains relatively insensitive to damping. For multilayer panels, the fluid-facing material determines the interfacial wave speed, while the subsurface stiffness distribution modifies the panel's effective thickness. Temporal stability analysis identifies regions of parameter space where a steady harmonic response is relevant and regions where instabilities grow.
